Commissioning management

Use the Navigator MC API to manage the commissioning of network elements.

The Commissioning API supports the following policy types:

  • For script generation of a homogeneous project only consisting of 6500 nodes: Public_IPV4_v1, Public_IPV6_v1 (6500-specific policies):

    This capability supports DCN Example 4 in the 6500 Packet-Optical Platform Data Communications Planning and User Guide, 323-1851-101. Private_IPV4_v1 (6500 specific policy, not supported in MCP 3.0) Public_IPV6_v1 (6500 specific policy)

  • For script generation of a homogeneous project only consisting of Waveserver nodes: Waveserver_v1.

  • For script generation of a homogeneous project only consisting of Waveserver5 nodes: Waveserver5_v1.

  • For script generation of a homogeneous project only consisting of RLS nodes: RLS_IPV4_v1.

  • For script generation of a heterogeneous project consisting of 6500 Waveserver and Waveserver5 nodes: Heterogeneous_v1.

  • For license configuration: License_6500_v1.

  • For SNMP configuration: SNMP_6500_v1.

  • For NTP configuration: NTP_Defaults_v1.

  • For 6500 equipment commissioning: EQPT_6500_v1.

  • For RADIUS servers configuration: Radius_Defaults_v1.

  • For craft user interface launch: Craft_UI_Launch_v1.

  • For ZTP configuration: ZTP_v1.

Related tasks, which are described later in this section, include:

  • Enabling Commissioning Script Generation Support

  • Policy management for script generation

  • Policy management for SNMP provisioning

  • Policy management for Heterogeneous project

  • Policy management for updating license server on network elements

  • Policy management for Waveserver script generation

  • Policy management for NTP provisioning

  • Policy management for RADIUS server provisioning

  • Policy management for ZTP provisioning

  • IP subnetwork management

  • Policy management for craft launch

Enabling Commissioning Script Generation Support

Script Generation Support in Navigator MC commissioning is by default Disabled, but it can be Enabled by updating the value of GCS Flag

By default, the value of GCS flag for Script Generation Support is False

Steps to Enable Script Generation Support

  1. Using the Navigator MC UI, select System > APIs.

    The System operations browser displays.

  2. Select Global Config Service in APIs

    The Global Config Service page displays.

  3. Select PUT API from config v1

    Global Config Service Config v1 PUT API

  4. Click on Try it out and add body with Value as "true"

  5. Sample request and body with GCS value as TRUE (to enable Script Support)

    1. Sample Request

    2. Sample Body (Initially, “Value” field will not be present)

      [
    {
        "application": "commissioning",
        "instance": "-",
        "name": "enable_script_support",
        "title": "Commissioning script generation support",
        "description": "Commissioning script generation support",
        "value": "true",
        "default": "false",
        "key": "commissioning/-/enable_script_support"
    }
]

  6. Execute the PUT API and Script Generation Support will be Enabled

Policy management for script generation

Use the Navigator MC API to manage policies for script generation.

Related tasks, which are described later in this section, include:

  • Set an active policy for script generation

  • Reset a policy to the defaults

Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project

To create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • As part of the call, you must provide the values for the new policy.

  • For the policyType, use a policy type supported for script generation. See Retrieve all policy types.

  • To set an active policy, set state to Active.

  • The following policy types are supported for 6500 nodes:

    • Private_IPV4_v1

    • Public_IPV4_v1

    • Public_IPV6_v1

  • The following policy types are supported for RLS nodes:

    • RLS_IPV4_v1

  • The following policy type is supported for Waveserver nodes:

    • Waveserver_v1.

  • The following policy type is supported for Waveserver5 nodes:

    • Waveserver5_v1.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policy/

Sample input to create a Public_IPV4_v1 policy

  {
   "policyName": "Policy01",
   "policyType": "Public_IPV4_v1",
   "description": "DCN routable policy",
   "customerName": "Telus",
   "state": "New"
  }

Sample response:

  {
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "policy_name": "Policy01",
          "state": "New",
          "supported_operation": "POST_SCRIPTS_v1",
          "description": "DCN routable policy",
          "customer_name": "telus"
        },
        "type": "Public_IPV4_v1",
        "id": "201ba295-3888-4b2d-9a4a-9d254de0c6a0"
      }
    ]
  }

Sample input to create a Public_IPV6_v1 policy

  {
   "policyName": "Policy06",
   "policyType": "Public_IPV6_v1",
   "description": "DCN routable policy",
   "customerName": "Telus",
   "state": "New"
  }

Sample response:

  {
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "policy_name": "Policy06",
          "state": "New",
          "supported_operation": "POST_SCRIPTS_v1",
          "description": "DCN routable policy",
          "customer_name": "telus"
        },
        "type": "Public_IPV6_v1",
        "id": "201ba295-3888-4b2d-9a4a-9d254de0c6a0"
      }
    ]
  }
The value for "id" in this response is used in a subsequent request.
Create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes project

To create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes project, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • As part of the call, you must provide the values for the new policy.

  • For the policyType, use a policy type supported for script generation. See Retrieve all policy types.

  • To activate the policy, set state to Active.

  • The following policy types are supported for 6500 nodes:

    • Private_IPV4_v1

    • Public_IPV4_v1

      • Support for NEMODE, ETHGFPRFI and Span Loss Margin is provided. The default values are: SONET for NEMODE, ENABLED for ETHGFPRFI, and 3 dB for Span Loss Margin.

    • Public_IPV6_v1

The following policy type is supported for Waveserver nodes: ** Waveserver_v1.

The following policy type is supported for Waveserver5 nodes: ** Waveserver5_v1.

The following policy type is supported for RLS nodes: ** RLS_IPV4_v1.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policy/

Sample input

  {
   "policyName": "Policy for 6500 and waveserver nodes projects",
   "policyType": "Heterogeneous_v1",
   "description": "Heterogeneous policy",
   "customerName": "AT&T",
   "state": "New"
  }

Sample response:

  {
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "policy_name": "Policy for 6500 and waveserver nodes projects",
          "state": "New",
          "supported_operation": "POST_SCRIPTS_v1",
          "description": "Heterogeneous policy",
          "customer_name": "AT&T"
        },
        "type": "Heterogeneous_v1",
        "id": "6802171a-e686-4cc2-8677-ea7cc8977133"
      }
    ]
  }
The value for "id" in this response is used in a subsequent request.
Retrieve all policies or a single policy

To retrieve all user policies or system policies, or any single policy, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • To retrieve all policies, leave the "id" parameter blank in the call.

  • To retrieve a single policy, include the "id" value in the call.

Sample request:

To retrieve all policies:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policy/

To retrieve a single policy:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policy/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Set an active policy for script generation

To set an active policy for script generation, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • Use a value for "id" as indicated in a response from Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project, Create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes project or Retrieve all policies.

  • Use a value for "policy" as indicated in the sample input.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policy/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Sample input

  {
   "state": "Active"
  }

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates a successful activation of a policy for script generation.

Retrieve policy data

To retrieve policy data, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • To retrieve all policies data, leave the "id" parameter blank.

  • To retrieve a single policy data, provide the "id" value.

Sample request:

To retrieve all policies' data:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/

To retrieve a single policy’s data:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Update a policy

To update a policy for script generation, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • Provide the "id" value obtained from Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project, Create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes project or from Retrieve all policies or a single policy.

  • Provide values for the defaults parameter obtained from Retrieve all policies or a single policy (that is, first GET the policy data, update the values as desired in that data, and then provide that updated data here under the defaults parameter).

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Reset a policy to the defaults

To set an active policy for script generation to the default values, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

Use a value for "id" as indicated in a response from Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project, Create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes project or Retrieve all policies.

Sample request:

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates a successful reset of the specified policy to default values.

Policy management for SNMP provisioning

To manage policies for SNMP provisioning, use the Commissioning API.

Related tasks, which are described below, include:

  • Retrieve the SNMP policy identifier. Perform Retrieve all policies or a single policy.

    The response identifies all of the policies available for commissioning. Within this response, locate the policy name Default Policy for 6500 SNMP 1. Record the value of the "id" parameter.

  • Retrieve SNMP policy data

  • Update SNMP policy data

Retrieve SNMP policy data

To retrieve SNMP policy data, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

Use the value of the "id" parameter you retrieved previously.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/?id=1b312740-d6b7-4aee-8037-744215515d52

Policy management for updating license server on network elements

Topics included in this section are:

  • Enabling the commissioning configuration policy for auto-update of LS IP to NEs (upon NE enrollment or resync or sync/discovery)

Enabling the commissioning configuration policy for automatic updates

Use the Commissioning API to enable the automatic distribution of license server data to NEs upon NE enrollment, resync, or sync/discovery.

License data audit/distribution can be triggered for all managed devices using the commissioning services API or from Swagger.

The API is: commissioning/api/v1/services/?deviceType=6500&service=license

You must set the values of the configuration policy’s "isRequired" and "overrideLicenseServer" attributes to True.

If you have only deployed 6500 NEs in your network, then the "isRequired" and "overrideLicenseServer" attribute values can remain False for productType: waveserver.

If the server uses HTTPS on port 7071, the protocol and port values can remain unchanged. The policy attribute needs to be changed if preAuth licenses are used by the customer on the device.

Retrieving the license policy You can retrieve the license policy using the Commissioning API as follows:

  1. In the Commissioning APIs, expand the PolicyDefaults V1 section.

  2. Run the GET call by setting the type parameter to License_Policy_v1.

  3. NOTE - GET response return by GET call contains id and type parameter of the policy, before passing GET response to body part of PUT call, Please remove these parameter.

  4. Run the PUT call and fill in the fields as follows:

    • id: copy and paste the "id" value from the above GET command response.

    • defaults: copy and paste the full response from the above GET command and then modify the values according to desired behaviour.

In the response, locate the license policy to find the UID for the license and its default data.

License server commissioning policy LicensePolicy types can be:

  • DEFAULT: Set the shelf feature licensing policy to follow the individual feature’s predefined policy.

  • STRICT: Enable shelf-wide, strict licensing policy for all features that can be overridden.

  • PREAUTH: Enable shelf-wide, pre-authorized licensing policy for all features that can be overridden.

LicensePolicy settings for 6500, RLS, WaveServer and WaveServer5 can be disabled by setting the "isRequired" attribute to False. Modifying the policy automatically causes the license server to distribute license data to all managed nodes. If required, the distribution of data can also be initiated using the Service API.

{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributes": {
        "additionalAttributes": {
          "data": {
            "license": {
              "policy": "DEFAULT",
              "products": [
                {
                  "isRequired": false,
                  "overrideLicenseServer": false,
                  "productType": "6500"
                },
                {
                  "isRequired": false,
                  "overrideLicenseServer": false,
                  "productType": "waveserver"
                },
                {
                  "isRequired": false,
                  "overrideLicenseServer": false,
                  "productType": "waveserver5"
                },
                 {
                  "productType": "RLS",
                  "isRequired": false,
                  "overrideLicenseServer": false
                }
              ],
              "protocol": "HTTPS",
              "server": {
                "port": {
                  "HTTP": "7072",
                  "HTTPS": "7071"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "License_Policy_v1",
      "id": "63a120f2-de41-495d-9ba3-46ce8b066d2b"
    }
  ]
}

Operational behavior

The following table describes the operational impact of the combined "isRequired" and "overrideLicenseServer" attributes in the licensing policy.

isRequired overrideLicenseServer Impact

True

False

Write to the node if no license server data is configured. If license server data is configured, do not modify the data.

True

True

1. Overwrite an existing NElicense server IP if the existing IP is not the same as the Navigator MC Site IP.

2. If the existing NE licenseserver IP is the same as the Navigator MC Site IP, do nothing.

False

True/False

You do not need to do anything.

Protocol and Ports

Port and Protocol is being deprecated. If the server uses HTTPS on port 7071 , the protocol and port values can remain unchanged.

The policy protocol defines the protocol to be used by the device to communicate to the licensing server. The default is to use HTTPS.

The port data defines the ports to use for the HTTP and HTTPS protocols. The default ports are:

  • HTTP: 7072

  • HTTPS: 7071

Updating the license attribute

Update the license attribute using the following PUT call:

Pass the UID and updated default Json in the call’s payload.

Use the commissioning services api to distribute the license server ip on the device commissioning/api/v1/services/?service=license. This will apply to all the devices which are enrolled in Navigator MC.

You can also distribute the license server ip to nodes of a specific type, for example 6500:

commissioning/api/v1/services/?service=license&deviceType=6500

Update ZTP policy data

To update ZTP policy data, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • Provide the "id" value obtained from Retrieve all policies or a single policy.

  • Provide values for the defaults parameter obtained from Retrieve ZTP policy data.

    To obtain these values, first GET the policy data and then provide this data to set ZTP DHCP server IPs, bootfile format and configFile format. Then assign these values to each product (for example, 6500 or Waveserver) here under the defaults parameter).

Relevant policy attributes The following are some of the attributes that the policy should hold to generate the ZTP boot and config file:

  • "productName": for 6500, this value is "6500"; for Waveserver, this value is "waveserver".

  • "configFileDirPath": the location of the config file on the FTP server.

  • "configFileRule" can have following values:

    • "retryOnFailure": the shelf decommissions itself and restarts the ZTP process if any commands fail to execute.

    • "ignoreOnFailure" (default value): the shelf completes the ZTP process even if some commands fail to execute.

    • "stopOnFailure": the shelf stops the ZTP process at the first failed command.

  • "ztpTimeout" (optional): specifies the time (in minutes) between retries. The default value is 60. The supported range is 30-1440. After three retries, the interval is set to 1440.

  • "filePrefix": the prefix is used when generating the Bootfile and Config file. Provide separate file prefix value for the bootfile and config file.

  • "fileSuffix": the suffix is the file extension used when generating the bootfile and ConfigFile. Provide separate file suffix values for the bootfile and config file.

  • "DHCPServers": the DHCP servers to be configured on each product.

  • "xmlSchema": the XML schema to be used for bootfiles.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/?id=e494e31b-8804-4bf7-9bd8-6bbf903ee9b1

Sample input

{
    "data": [
        {

                "additionalAttributes": {
                    "data": {
                        "ztp": {
                            "products": [
                                {
                                    "bootFile": {
                                        "filePrefix": "bootfile_6500",
                                        "configFileDirPath": "/ZTP_6500/CLI",
                                        "fileSuffix": ".xml",
                                        "productName": "6500",

                                        "configFileRule": "ignoreOnFailure"
                                    },

                                        "fileSuffix": ".txt",
                                        "filePrefix": "config_6500",
                                        "namingStrategy": "NONE"
                                    },
                                    "productType": "6500",
                                    "dhcpServerReferences": [
                                        {
                                            "dhcpServerKey": "S1"
                                        }
                                    ]
                                },
                                {
                                    "bootFile": {
                                        "filePrefix": "bootfile_6500",
                                        "configFileDirPath": "/ZTP_WS",
                                        "fileSuffix": ".xml",
                                        "productName": "waveserver",
                                        "xmlSchema": "ciena",
                                        "ztpTimeoutInMin": "60",
                                        "operation": "",
                                        "configFileRule": "activate"
                                    },

                                    },

                                        }

                                },

                                        "configFileDirPath": "/myconfigdir",
                                        "fileSuffix": ".xml",
                                        "productName": "8180",

IP subnetwork management

To manage an IPv4 or IPv6 subnetwork, use the Commissioning API.

Related tasks include:

  • Allocate an IP subnetwork

  • Retrieve an IP subnetwork

  • Delete an IP subnetwork

  • Disable IPSubnet Validation

  • Load Reserved Shelf IP Data

  • Retrieve Reserved Shelf IP Data

  • Delete Reserved Shelf IP Data

  • Retrieve the IP address from a subnet or TID

Allocate an IP subnetwork

To allocate a IPv4 or IPv6 subnetwork and OspfArea for the shelf of 6500 network elements, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • Provide the "IP value" with CIDR.

  • Provide the "ospfArea".

  • Provide the "IP6" value with CIDR.

  • Provide the "ospfAreaV3".

  • Provide the "type".

IPSubnet creation body

  {
    "data": {
        "attributes": {
          "IP": "string",
          "ospfArea": "string",
          "ospfAreav3": "string",
          "IP6": "string"
        },
        "type": "string"
    }
  }

Replace the following parameters as required:

  • "IP" (string): a range of IPv4 addresses used to allocate the shelf IPv4 address in commissioning (for example, 147.23.24.24)

  • "IP6" (string): a range of IPv6 addresses used to allocate the shelf IPv6 address in commissioning (for example, 2081::4)

  • "CIDR" (string): number of IP addresses under the IPSubnet (for example, 22)

  • "OspfArea" (string): OspfAreaV2 of the IPSubnet (for example, 0.0.0.3)

  • "OspfAreaV3" (string): OspfAreaV3 of the IPSubnet

  • "type" (string): an optional parameter. If this parameter is not provided, shelf is the default. Other possible values include Craft, which is used for craft.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/ipsubnet/

Sample response:

A response code of 201 indicates successful creation of the IPv4 or IPv6 subnetwork.

Retrieve an IP subnetwork

To retrieve details about an allocated IP subnetwork, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before making this call, perform Allocate an IP subnetwork.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/ipsubnet/

Sample response:

  {
    "data": [
        {
            "attribute": {
                 "IP": [
                     "10.183.0.0/22"
                     "1,2"
                 ],
                 "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0"
             },
             "type": "shelf",
             "id": "9591f3b2-251f-4e45-9e90-34451f3e7c0"
         },
         {

             "attribute": {
                 "IP": [
                     "2081::4/22"
                     "1,2"
                 ],
                 "ospfArea": "0.0.0.3"
             },
             "type": "shelf",
             "id": "838a1be9-15b6-42c6-880f-f4bf3a29d304"
         }
     }
  }
Delete an IP subnetwork

To delete an IPv4 or IPv6 subnetwork, use the Commissioning API.

You can only delete those subnets which do not contain any shelf IP addresses.

Requirements

Before making this call, perform Allocate an IP subnetwork.

Elements of the call

  • Provide the ospfArea value obtained from Retrieve an IP subnetwork.

  • Provide the subnetId value obtained from Retrieve an IP subnetwork.

IPSubnet deletion body

  {
      "subnetId": "[SUBNETID]",
      "ospfArea": "[OSPFAREA]"
  }

Replace the following parameters as required:

  • "subnetId (string): a unique identifier retrieved from Retrieve an IP subnetwork. For example, "ccff736d-4e7f-4752-8531-f1b180219f61".

  • ospfArea (string): the IP address of the OspfArea to be deleted (for example, 0.0.0.2)

Sample request:

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/ipsubnet/

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates successful creation of the IP subnetwork.

Load Reserved Shelf IP Data

There are shelves on the network which are already deployed and assigned IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. Use this API to reserve shelf IPv4 or IPv6 data in commissioning.

Use the Commissioning API to reserve shelf IPv4 or IPv6 network data for 6500 devices during commissioning. To load the shelves IP data, post an API call as shown below with a body resembling the sample provided.

Sample request:

POST{NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/reservedIP/

Elements of the call

Substitute values for the following parameters within the sample body shown below:

  • "shelfNumber" (string): the shelf number, for example 1

  • "projectId" (string): the Navigator MC Project ID

  • "ospfAreaV3" (string): the IP address of the OspfAreaV3

  • "ospfArea" (string): the IP address of the OspfAreaV2 (for example, 0.0.0.2)

  • "IP6" (string): the reserved IPV6Address of the shelf

  • "IP" (string): the reserved IPV4Address of the shelf

  • "tid" (string): the Target Identifier

  • "type" (string): the default value is "shelf"

  • "projectName": the Navigator MC Project Name

Reserve IP Address body

  [
    {
      "shelfNumber": "string",
      "projectId": "string",
      "ospfAreaV3": "string",
      "ospfArea": "string",
      "IP6": "string",
      "IP": "string",
      "tid": "string",
      "type": "string",
      "projectName": "string"
    }
  ]

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates successful reservation of the IP subnetwork.

Retrieve Reserved Shelf IP Data

To to retrieve the reserved Shelf IP data, use the Commissioning API.

Requirement

Before making this call, you should have invoked Load Reserved Shelf IP Data.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/reservedIP/?tid=<tid>

Elements of the call

In the call, provide a value for the "tid" parameter. This is the tid (Target Identifier) of the deployed shelf with an IP Address.

Sample response:

{
    "ospfArea": "0.0.0.3",
    "projectName": "",
    "projectid": "",
    "shelfIP": "2018::1",
    "shelfNumber": "1",
    "tid": "sidtid1",
    "usage": "shelf"
}
{
    "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0",
    "projectName": "",
    "projectid": "",
    "shelfIP": "10.183.0.1",
    "shelfNumber": "1",
    "tid": "sidtid1",
    "usage": "shelf"
}
Delete Reserved Shelf IP Data

To delete the Reserved Shelf IP data, use the Commissioning API.

Requirement

Before making this call, you should have invoked Load Reserved Shelf IP Data.

Elements of the call

Substitute values for the following parameters in the sample body below:

  • "TargetIdentifier" (string): the Target Identifier of the deployed shelf (for example, "MALTON")

  • "ShelfNumber" (string): the shelf number (for example, "3")

Sample request:

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v2/reservedIP/

{
    "tid": "[TargetIdentifier]",
    "shelfNumber": "[ShelfNumber]"
}

A response code of 200 indicates that reserved shelf was successfully deleted.

Disable IPSubnet Validation

To disable IPSubnet validation use the Global Config Service API. IPAddress for the shelf is reserved without IPSubnet in commissioning.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/gcs/api/v1/config

[
  {
    "application": "commissioning",
    "instance": "-",
    "partition": "commissioning",
    "name": "disable.ipsubnet.validation",
    "title": "disable.ipsubnet.validation",
    "value": "true"
  }
]
In above sample request the values are case sensitive. It is recommended that not to change these values after setting the IPSubnet Validation.

IPSubnet Validation can also be disabled from UI→System→Configuration(ApplicationConfiguration)

Policy management for craft launch

To manage policies for launching a network element’s craft interface, use the Commissioning API.

Related tasks include:

  • Retrieve the craft policy

  • Update the craft policy to identify the location of the 6500 Site Manager software

Requirements

Before managing craft launch policies, the 6500 Site Manager software must be installed on a known server.

For more information about installing 6500 Site Manager, see the Navigator NCS Installation Guide.

Retrieve the craft launch policy

Retrieve the craft launch policy using the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

Within the call, include "Craft_UI_Launch_v1" as the value of the "type" parameter.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/

Sample response:

  {
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "additionalAttributes": {
            "data": {
              "craftLaunch": {
                "nodes": [
                 {
                  "attributes": {
                   "server": "Site_Manager_GUI_Server_host_name",
                   "craftFolder": "sitemanager",
                   "port": "8443",
                   "preferredProtocol": "https",
                   "craftLaunchLabel": "Site manager"
                 },
                 "nodeType": "6500"
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      },
      "type": "Craft_UI_Launch_v1",
      "id": "706d670e-9724-4a02-92bb-7a13957f7496"
     }
   ]
  }
Update the craft policy to identify the location of the 6500 Site Manager software

To update the craft launch policy to identify the location of the 6500 Site Manager software, use the Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

  • Provide the "id" value obtained from Retrieve the craft policy.

  • Using the response from Retrieve the craft policy, replace the value of the "server" attribute (nodeType="6500" and craftLaunchLabel="Site manager") with the hostname or IP address of the server that is hosting the 6500 Site Manager software.

    In the sample input below, 'Site_Manager_GUI_Server_host_name' has been replaced with hostname 'halifax02'. . NOTE - GET response return by GET call contains id and type parameter of the policy, before passing GET response to body part of PUT call, Please remove these parameter. Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/policyDefaults/

Sample input

  {
    "data": [
      {
        "attributes": {
          "additionalAttributes": {
            "data": {
              "craftLaunch": {
                "nodes": [
                 {
                  "attributes": {
                   "server": "halifax02",
                   "craftFolder": "sitemanager",
                   "port": "8443",
                   "preferredProtocol": "https",
                   "craftLaunchLabel": "Site manager"
                 },
                 "nodeType": "6500"
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      }
     }
   ]
  }

Sample response:

A response code of 201 indicates that the craft launch policy was successfully updated.

Retrieve the IP address from a subnet or TID

To retrieve the IP address from a subnet or TID, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you invoke the request, perform either of the following:

  • Reserve the IP address by performing Load Reserved Shelf IP Data.

  • Generate the commissioning scripts.

Sample request - IP address from TID:

In the call, specify the Target Identifier (TID).

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/ipaddress/?tid={TID}

Sample response::

{
    "MALTON": [
        {
            "ipaddress": "2091::1",
            "ospfArea": "3.0.0.0",
            "shelfNumber": "1"
        },
        {
            "ipaddress": "20.0.0.2",
            "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0",
            "shelfNumber": "2"
        },
        {
            "ipaddress": "2091::2",
            "ospfArea": "3.0.0.0",
            "shelfNumber": "2"
        },
        {
            "ipaddress": "20.0.0.1",
            "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0",
            "shelfNumber": "1"
        }
    ]
}

Sample request — IP address from subnet:

As part of the call, specify the subnet with CIDR used during subnet allocation.

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/ipaddress/?subnet={SUBNET}

Sample response::

{
    "subnet": [
        {
            "tid": "MALTON",
            "shelfNumber": "2",
            "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0",
            "ipaddress": "20.0.0.2"
        },
        {
            "tid": "MALTON",
            "shelfNumber": "1",
            "ospfArea": "2.0.0.0",
            "ipaddress": "20.0.0.1"
        }
    ]
}

Generate the commissioning scripts

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

  • committed a fiber route planning project.

  • check if script generation is supported

  • set the following:

    • IP address

    • the name

    • the user data

  • created a RADIUS profile to add the primary and secondary RADIUS server details. You do not need to perform this procedure for each project.

  • set an active policy for scripts generation and the policy data.

  • allocated shelf IPv4 subnets.

  • configured SNMP policy data.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • optionally, the value of the "policyid". The specified commissioning policy will be used to generate commissioning scripts.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

                      "format": "ztpScripts"
                  },
                  {
                      "link": "https://NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/?projectname=GfDeg1&devicetype=6500",
                      "format": "json"
                  }
              ]
          }
      ],
      "projectName": "GfDeg1",
      "nodes": [
          {
              "deviceType": "6500",
              "shelves": [
                  {
                      "release": "12.1",
                      "shelfId": "1",
                      "primary": "Enable"
                  }
              ],
              "nodeType": "OADM",
              "nodeName": "sidtid1",
              "scriptLinks": [
                  {
                      "link": "https://NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/?projectname=GfDeg1&devicetype=6500&nodename=sidtid1",
                      "format": "json"
                  },
                  {
                      "link": "https://NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/?projectname=GfDeg1&devicetype=6500&nodename=sidtid1&format=ztpScripts",
                      "format": "ztpScripts"
                  }
              ]
          },
          {
              "deviceType": "6500",
              "shelves": [
                  {
                      "release": "12.1",
                      "shelfId": "1",
                      "primary": "Enable"
                  }
              ],
              "nodeType": "OADM",
              "nodeName": "sidtid2",
              "scriptLinks": [

                      "link": "https://NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/?projectname=GfDeg1&devicetype=6500&nodename=sidtid2",

                  {
                      "link": "https://NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/?projectname=GfDeg1&devicetype=6500&nodename=sidtid2&format=ztpScripts",

The sample POST response shown above contains the link to the scripts instead of scripts in earlier version of commissioning. Copy the contents of the response and save it to a text file with the extension .json.
To apply a commissioning script to an NE, follow the procedure for "Commissioning via a script" in the 6500 Packet Optical Platform Commissioning and Testing, 323-1851-221, Issue 3 or later customer documentation.

Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (6500)

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

  • committed a fiber route or equipment planning project.

  • check if script generation is supported

  • set the following:

    • IP address

    • the name

    • the user data

  • configured RADIUS policy data to add the primary and secondary RADIUS server details. The RADIUS policy must be set to active. You do not need to perform this procedure for each project.

  • set an active policy for scripts generation and the policy data.

  • allocated shelf IPv4 subnets.

  • configured SNMP policy data.

  • if you want propagation of TID to L0 OSRP name then enable this using GCS(Global Configuration API)

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/gcs/api/v1/config

[
  {
    "application": "nsi",
    "partition": "nsi",
    "instance": "-",
    "name": "enable.tid.namePropagate",
    "title": "enable.tid.namePropagate",
    "description": "Enabling the flag for testing",
    "value": "true",
    "default": "false"
  }
]

  • From Navigator MC UI→System→Configuration (Application Configuration)

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter in the text box. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • the value of the "policyid" to in the text box. The specified commissioning policy will be used to generate commissioning scripts.

A policy for one of the following policy types can be used to generate scripts for 6500 nodes: * Private_IPV4_v1 * Public_IPV4_v1 * Public_IPV6_v1

To create the policy, see Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project.

Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (RLS)

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

    • IP address

    • the name

  • configured NTP, License policy data to add the NTP, License server details. You do not need to perform this procedure for each project.

Generate commissioning scripts for a heterogeneous project (6500, RLS, Waveserver and Waveserver5)

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

  • committed a fiber route or equipment planning project.

  • check if script generation is supported

  • set the following:

    • IP address

    • the name

    • the user data

  • configured RADIUS policy data to add the primary and secondary RADIUS server details. The RADIUS policy must be set to active. You do not need to perform this procedure for each project.

  • Set policies data for following policy types:

    • 6500 node policy (Private_IPV4_v1 or Public_IPV4_v1 or Public_IPV6_v1)

    • Waveserver node policy (Waveserver_v1)

    • Waveserver5 node policy (Waveserver5_v1)

    • RLS node policy (RLS_IPV4_v1)

    • heterogeneous policy (Heterogeneous_v1)

      To create node-specific policy, see Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project.

      To create a heterogeneous policy, see Create a policy for script generation of a heterogeneous nodes

  • set an active heterogeneous policy for scripts generation and policy data. In the heterogeneous policy data, set policyid for:

    • a 6500 node. Policy type for this can be Private_IPV4_v1 or Public_IPV4_v1 or Public_IPV6_v1

    • a Waveserver node

    • a Waveserver5 node

    • a RLS node

  • allocated shelf IPv4 subnets.

  • configured SNMP policy data.

  • for propagation of TID to L0 OSRP Name see before you start section Create a policy for script generation of a homogeneous nodes project.

  • For 6500 managed via RLS

    • In the 6500 script policy, the shelfRouting shall be configured as iISIS.

      If the 6500 script policy shelfRouting is configured as OSPF, the configuration will not build correctly.

    • Commissioning will configure OSPF for the 6500 port connected to the RLS.

    • Commissioning will configure OSPF for the RLS port connected to the 6500.

    • The 6500 port connected to the RLS shall be unnumbered.

    • The RLS port connected to the 6500 shall be unnumbered.

  • For Waveserver/Waveserver5 managed via RLS

    • The RLS port connected to the Waveserver must be numbered.

    • The IP subnet assigned to the RLS port must be sized to encompass all subtended Waveservers.

    • There must be a passive OSPF circuit assigned to the RLS port connected to the Waveserver. Commissioning will automatically do this.

    • The Waveserver DCN port must be connected to the RLS.

    • All Waveserver devices connected to the same or different RLS devices must be in different IP subnet.

Elements of the call:

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • the value of the "policyid" parameter. The specified commissioning policy will be used to generate commissioning scripts.

A policy for the following policy type can be used to generate scripts for a heterogeneous nodes project: Heterogeneous_v1.

Generate commissioning scripts for brownfield projects

Brownfield adds support for augmenting discovered networks by adding additional degrees, add/drop.

Due to not having all of the discovered nodes comms information available, a brownfield augment will not include comms configuration operations such as:

No turning up of an OSC, ILAN or COLAN on any existing node which is being augmented.

In the scenario where a new node is being deployed and it requires OSC/ILAN connectivity to an existing node, the OSC/ILAN on the existing node will not be turned up in the augment script generated for the existing node.

The user will need to manually enter the commands for OSC/ILAN connectivity.

Retrieve the commissioning scripts

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you retrieve the commissioning scripts, make sure that you Generate the commissioning scripts.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • optionally, parameter "devicetype" which specifies the device type planned network (6500, Waveserver).

  • optionally, parameter "nodename" which identifies the specific device in a planned network.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Sample response for 6500:

{
  "data": {
    "nodes": [
      {
        "nodeType": "OADM",
        "deviceType": "6500",
        "nodeName": "sidtid1",
        "shelves": [
          {
            "shelfId": "1",
            "primary": "Enable",
            "scripts": [
              {
                "release": "12.1",
                "sequenceId": "1",
                "commands": [
                  {
                    "commandType": "comment",
                    "command": "\\\"This TL1 Script was created with Commissioning MicroService for: { \"DeviceType\":\"6500\", \"NodeType\":\"OADM\", \"TID\":\"sidtid1\", \"Shelf\": \"1\", \"FIC\": \"fic_NE1_Shelf1\", \"Primary\": \"Enable\", \"Release\":\"12.1\", \"Timestamp\":\"2018-02-21_11-41-41-862000\", \"FileName\":\"6500_sidtid1-SHELF-1_1.bch\", \"relatedProjects\":\"\"} \"\\;"
                  },
                  {
                    "commandType": "macro",
                    "command": "\\\"PROMPT= Please confirm configuring node: sidtid1, Shelf: 1, FIC: fic_NE1_Shelf1 and Release: 12.1\"\\;"
                  },
                  {
                    "commandType": "tl1",
                    "command": "SET-SID:GenTID1:SHELF-0:1::\"sidtid1\";"
                  },
                  {
                    "commandType": "tl1",
                    "command": "ENT-SHELF:sidtid1:SHELF-1:1:::SITEID=1,SITENAME=\"Site1\",,FIC=\"fic_NE1_Shelf1\",,,,,,,PRIMARY=Enable,TIDC=Enable,EXTENDEDSHELF=DISABLE,,;"
                  },
                  {
                    "commandType": "macro",
                    "command": "\\\"Set Current Date and Time\"\\;"
                  },

To apply a commissioning script to an 6500 NE, follow the procedure for "Commissioning via a script" in the 6500 Packet Optical Platform Commissioning and Testing, 323-1851-221, Issue 3 or later customer documentation. If Network Element name changes after generating the scripts, the scripts will be deleted as part of name change events. You will then need to re-generate the scripts.

Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (6500)

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you retrieve the commissioning scripts, ensure that you Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of 6500 nodes.

You can also retrieve scripts using links provided for each node in the response from Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of 6500 nodes.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

To apply a commissioning script to a network element, see "Commissioning via a script" in 6500 Packet Optical Platform Commissioning and Testing, 323-1851-221, Issue 3 or later.

Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (RLS)

To generate commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you retrieve the commissioning scripts, ensure that you Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of RLS nodes.

You can also retrieve scripts using links provided for each node in the response from Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of RLS nodes.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Copy the contents of the response and save it to a text file with the extension .json.

To apply a commissioning script to a network element, see "Commissioning via a script" in 6500 Packet Optical Platform Commissioning and Testing, 323-1851-221, Issue 3 or later.

Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (Waveserver)

To retrieve commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

  • generated commissioning scripts as described in Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of Waveserver nodes.

  • provided a commissioning script for a node consisting of the CLI commands required to commission a Waveserver node.

  • saved this script in a file and executed it on a Waveserver at the CLI prompt.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • the value of the "devicetype" as Waveserver.

  • a value for "nodename".

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Sample response:

\"This CLI Script was created with Commissioning MicroService for: {"DeviceType":"WaveserverAi", "NodeType":"", "NodeName":"WS2", "Shelf": "1", "Primary": "Enable", "Release":"", "Timestamp":"2017-11-29_14-01-06-626000", "FileName":"WS_WS2_1.bch"} "\;
software show
system set member-id 5 site-id 12 host-name WSAi1 group-id 6 member-name WSAi1
system set site-longitude 78.43621 site-latitude 23.9769
configuration save
dhcp client disable
interface set  interface local ip 10.11.12.13/255.255.255.250
interface set  gateway 10.20.30.40
configuration save
ntp client set polling-interval 16
ntp client set mode polling
ntp client add server 0.0.0.0:1
ntp client enable server 0.0.0.0:1
configuration save

Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project (Waveserver5)

To retrieve commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have:

  • generated commissioning scripts as described in Generate commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of Waveserver5 nodes.

  • provided a commissioning script for a node consisting of the CLI commands required to commission a Waveserver5 node.

  • saved this script in a file and executed it on a Waveserver5 at the CLI prompt.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • the value of the "devicetype" as Waveserver5.

  • a value for "nodename".

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Sample response:

\"This CLI Script was created with Commissioning MicroService for: {"DeviceType":"Waveserver5", "NodeType":"", "NodeName":"WS2", "Shelf": "1", "Primary": "Enable", "Release":"", "Timestamp":"2017-11-29_14-01-06-626000", "FileName":"WS_WS2_1.bch"} "\;
software show
system set member-id 5 site-id 12 host-name WS5_1 group-id 6 member-name WS5_1
system set site-longitude 78.43621 site-latitude 23.9769
configuration save
dhcp client disable
interface set  interface local ip 10.11.12.13/255.255.255.250
interface set  gateway 10.20.30.40
configuration save
ntp client set polling-interval 16
ntp client set mode polling
ntp client add server 0.0.0.0:1
ntp client enable server 0.0.0.0:1
configuration save

Retrieve commissioning scripts for a heterogeneous project (6500, RLS, Waveserver and Waveserver5)

To retrieve commissioning scripts, use the Commissioning API.

Requirements

Before you start, make sure that you have generated commissioning scripts as described in Generate commissioning scripts for a heterogeneous project consisting of 6500 nodes, RLS, Waveserver nodes and Waveserver5 nodes.

You can also retrieve scripts using links provided for each node in the response from Generate commissioning scripts for a heterogeneous project consisting of 6500 nodes, RLS, Waveserver nodes and Waveserver5 nodes.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide:

  • the value of the "projectname" parameter. This specifies the project name of the planned network in RPT.

  • the value of the "devicetype" as Waveserver.

  • a value for "nodename".

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/scripts/

Sample response (for a 6500 node script)

Refer to the sample response in Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of 6500 nodes.

Sample response (for a Waveserver node script)

Refer to the sample response in Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of Waveserver nodes.

Sample response (for a RLS node script)

Refer to the sample response in Retrieve commissioning scripts for a homogeneous project only consisting of RLS nodes.

Create the commissioning scripts to configure 6500 eMOTR cards

Navigator MC provides commissioning capabilities through a custom script framework to create and run custom scripts to configure the following for 6500-S Release 12.3:

  • eMOTR / eMOTR Edge i/f card TL/1 interface

  • eMOTR / eMOTR Edge i/f card SAOS CLI interface

The following related topics are included below:

  • Retrieve shelf/group information for the 6500 device

  • Native script - Provisioning

  • Native script - Retrieval

  • Custom script

Retrieve shelf-group info for the 6500 device

Sample request:

Use the Network Element Configuration API to retrieve information about the configured shelf-group in a 6500 device.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs/

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "shelfEquipmentgroupShow",
          "inputs": [
            {}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}",
        "typeGroup": "{{NE_TYPEGROUP}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Native script - Provisioning

Use the Network Element Configuration API to invoke the request.

Provisioning includes creating, editing, and deleting.

For 6500 devices "shelf" and "group" are mandatory parameters. The correct location to provide "shelf" and "group" is within "input" as shown in below example:- 
{
  "data": {
      "type": "jobs",
      "attributes": {
        "maxConnections": "10",
        "scheduleTime": "2017-03-23T14:54:06.000+0000",
          "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "{{SCRIPT_NAME}}",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [],
              "shelf": "{{SHELF}}",
              "group": "{{GROUP}}"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
      }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME_6500}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME_6500}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Elements of the call

As part of the call, provide values for the "shelf" and "group" parameters.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs/

{
  "data": {
      "type": "jobs",
      "attributes": {
        "maxConnections": "10",
        "scheduleTime": "2017-03-23T14:54:06.000+0000",
          "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "lagConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                     "action": "create",
                     "aggName":"agg_test",
                     "primaryPorts": "3/2"
                  }
                }
              ],
              "shelf": "1",
              "group": "41"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
      }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Native script - Retrieval

Use the Network Element Configuration API to invoke the request.

For 6500 devices "shelf" and "group" are mandatory parameters. The correct location to provide "shelf" and "group" is within "input" as shown in below example:-

Elements of the call

Custom script

When running a custom script, you normally identify the shelf and group of the target equipment as part of the commands to be run using a CLI interface.

For a 6500 device, when using a CLI protocol, shelf and group information will be provided as part of script inputs. These inputs are not mandatory; if they are absent, the script is run on the first shelf/group.

Error scenario and back default behaviour (when shelf/ eqpt-group information is not provided) is Retrieve information from all eqpt-group.

Error scenario and backward compatibility behaviour

If the shelf/group are not provided in the profile or userData, the operation will not be aborted and no message will be provided. When shelf/group information is not provided, the CLI commands will be executed on the first shelf/group. NE errors will be populated.

Custom script - commands

{
    "data": {
        "type": "jobs",
        "attributes": {
            "maxConnections": 10,
            "scheduleTime": "2016-07-02T15:04:06Z",
            "scripts": [
                {
                    "scriptName": "cliCutThrough",

                    "inputs": [
                        {
                            "commands": [
                                "port set port 2/1 description {{description}} \n"
                            ],
                            "shelf":"1",
                            "group":"41"

                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        },
    },
    "included": [
        {
            "id": "{{device_name}}",
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "attributes": {
                "ipAddress": "{{device_name}}"
            }
        }
    ]
}

Custom script - cmdFile, userData, Profiles

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": 10,
      "scheduleTime": "2016-07-02T15:04:06Z",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "cliCutThrough",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "cmdFile": "ciena6500Scriptcli",
              "protocolType": "cli",
              "shelf": "1",
              "group": "41"
            }
          ],
          "relationships": {
            "profile": {
              "data": {
                "type": "profiles",
                "id": "0"
              }
            },
            "userdata": {
              "data": {
                "type": "userdatas",
                "id": "0"
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{SESSION_ID_6500}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME_6500}}"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "profiles",
      "id": "0",
      "attributes": {
        "profileName": "ciena6500Profilecli"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "userdatas",
      "id": "0",
      "attributes": {
        "description": "cienatest"
      }
    }
  ]
}

eMOTR card

A 6500 device may contain multiple eMOTR cards or XC cards, or a combination of XC and eMOTR cards on the same shelf with a different equipment group. Different cards can be on a different shelf and in different eqpipment groups.

The eMOTR card works in two threads: L2-STANDARD and L2_EXTENDED. L2_STANDARD is a QinQ-only mode with no support for MPLS.

Assumptions

  • This operation does not differentiate between the XC and eMOTR cards, or between eMOTR / eMOTR Edge i/f cards.

  • This operation does not differentiate between L2-STANDARD and L2_EXTENDED cards. If MPLS is not supported, Navigator MC will populate NE errors for any MPLS CLI commands.

Service provisioning after commissioning

When no errors occur during network element commissioning, services are automatically provisioned after successful discovery of the network element. However, if errors occur during the provisioning of these services, you can manually trigger service provisioning.

Tasks include:

  1. Manually trigger service provisioning

  2. Retrieve the service state

  3. Retrieve management sessions

Requirements

Before you begin, make sure that you have:

  • If required, set the trap destination in the commissioning SNMP policy data.

  • If required, configured the SNMP defaults in the commissioning SNMP policy defaults.

Manually trigger service provisioning

Manually trigger service provisioning after automated service provisioning has failed using the following Commissioning API.

Elements of the call

Provide the value of the session_id parameter in the text box. This value specifies the management "session_id" for the NE. You retrieve the management session_id using the instructions in section Retrieve management sessions.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/commissioning/api/v1/services/

Sample input

  {
         "session_id": "148e227f-1962-4b4d-ba59-dc9b12627ac6"
  }

Sample response:

A response code of 201 indicates successful service provisioning of the services. A response code of 202 indicates that the request is accepted and will be processed in the background.

Change a network element connection profile

You can use the Navigator MC API to change the Navigator MC security profile for a pre-enrolled or enrolled network element.

The network element connection profile contains device credentials and connection ports to the network element.

The changed profile takes effect the next time the Navigator MC server connects to the network element. Specific updates include:

  • Change credentials in the network element profile.

  • For devices with failover paths, such as dual GNE, the updated profile is used when a failure occurs.

  • For devices without failover paths, the updated profile is only used if the device is manually resynchronized once it has gone LOA or force-reconnect Otherwise, the RA uses cached credentials.

Use the Management Sessions API to change the network element connection profile.

Requirements

The network element must already be pre-enrolled or enrolled.

Sample request:

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/discovery/api/v4/managementSessions/{sessionId}

  {
  	"operations" : [
  		{
  			"op": "replace",
  			"attributes": {
  			   "profile" : "<NE_PROFILE_ID>"
  			   }
  		}]
  }

Sample response:

  {
  	"data": {
  		"id": "32c3c340-d9b8-49a7-b7dd-22dced75985d",
  		"type": "managementSessions",
  		"attributes": {
  			"displayData": {
  				"displayState": "CONNECTED"
  			},
  			"ipAddress": "10.182.191.170",
  			"typeGroup": "CienaWaveserver",
  			"name": "US-IL-Midway-WS001",
  			"profile": "8d65b066-46c9-4da4-8a86-cbf173b2f65a",
  			. . .
  		}
  	}
  }

Commission and configure a node or port

To commission and configure a node or port, use the Network Element Configuration API.

The following samples relate to 8700.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, specify values for the following attributes:

  • "maxConnections": the maximum number of connections.

  • "scheduleTime: the time at which to execute the job.

  • "scriptName": the name of the script to execute. In this example, it is the portConfig script.

    The scriptname varies for different commissioning, as follows:

    • for a port: "portConfig"

    • for a port interface: "portInterfaceConfig"

    • for a node: "nodeConfig"

  • "profileName": the profile name.

  • "type": type of job (for example, job).

  • "action": specifies the type of actions (create, delete) that can be performed on the script (in this example, it is create).

  • "neName": the network element name.

  • "neType": the network element type.

Sample request:

For 6500 devices "shelf" and "group" are mandatory parameters. The correct location to provide "shelf" and "group" is within "input" as shown in below example:- 
{
  "data": {
      "type": "jobs",
      "attributes": {
        "maxConnections": "10",
        "scheduleTime": "2017-03-23T14:54:06.000+0000",
          "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "{{SCRIPT_NAME}}",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [],
              "shelf": "{{SHELF}}",
              "group": "{{GROUP}}"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
      }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME_6500}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME_6500}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Specify traffic engineering parameters for an IP interface

To specify the traffic engineering parameters for an IP interface, use the Network Element Configuration API.

The following samples relate to SRLG.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, specify values for the following attributes:

  • "Region Id": describes region component. The first 6 bits are allocated for region.

  • "Type": describes risk type component. Bits 7-10 are allocated for risk type.

  • "Summary Bit": identifies the summary bit. Bit 11 is allocated for the summary bit.

    • When the Summary Bit is 0, Navigator MC will never automatically overwrite

    • when the Summary Bit is 1, Navigator MC will automatically overwrite once propagation from lower layers is supported

  • "Risk value": Identifies the risk value bits. The lower 21 bits are allocated for risk values

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Example

A manually-entered ROADM Degree risk against an IP interface:

  • 0x19E001E3 (0001,10 01,11 1 0,0000,0000,0001,1110,0011)

    • Region Id = 6 (assuming controllerId.value will be set to 6)

    • Summary Bit = 1 (so Navigator MC will automatically overwrite once propagation from lower layers is supported)

    • Risk id = 483

Allocated bits update process

SRLG value bits are configured in an RA container. This can be modified by modifying the values in commissioning_properties.py file.

REGION_ID_BIT_ALLOCATION = '6' # CONTROLLER_ID

RISK_TYPE_BIT_ALLOCATION = '4' # TYPE

RISK_SUMMARY_BIT_ALLOCATION = '1' # SUMMARY

RISK_VALUE_BIT_ALLOCATION = '21' # RISK_VALUE

Use the following CLI command to set SRLG:

mpls traffic-engg set ip-interface <interface_name> srlg <srlg_value>

Request payload for updating values

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "portInterfaceConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "update",
                    "srlgRegionId": 6,
                    "srlgRiskType": 7,
                    "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
                    "srlgRiskValue": 483,
                    "linkCost": 200
                    "interfaceName": "if",
                    "resourceColorGroupName": "tdm_color_gr"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}"
          }
        ]

    }
  },
  "included": [

      "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",

        "ncId": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",

        "ipAddress": "{{NE_IP_ADDRESS}}",
        "neType": "{{NE_TYPE}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Retrieve health diagnostics from a node

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve information from individual nodes pertaining to the node’s "health". This includes information about the node’s state that is not directly related to services and connections like temperature, CPU usage, and so on.

SAOS 8x platforms maintain extensive health tracking records, monitoring almost every single aspect of the chassis.

SAOS 6x platforms maintain more limited records focused on key data.

Information for SAOS 6.x nodes

SAOS 6x platforms maintain records of key data such as temperature, CPU state, and memory usage. This includes:

  • cpu load average

  • cpu utilization

  • memory utilization

  • temperature

  • power

Information for SAOS 8.x nodes

SAOS 8x platforms mmaintain elaborate health tracking for almost every single aspect of the chassis.

  • 8700 devices support the following health item categories:

    • CPU

    • memory usage

    • power

    • temperature

  • 6500 devices support the following health item categories:

    • CPU

    • memory usage

API calls to retrieve node health information

Use the JOB POST REST API of Network Element Configuration in Navigator MC to invoke requests:

/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Include the following parameters in your request:

  • Attributes: healthitem

  • Type: string

  • Values: temperature

  • Script Name: HealthDiagnosticShow

The following examples show sample API calls requesting health diagnostics for both 6500 and 8700 nodes.

Display health diagnostic for temperature on a SAOS 6x device

Sample request:

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "healthDiagnosticShow",
          "inputs": [
            {
                "healthitem": "temperature"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "{{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}}",
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}",
        "ipAddress": "{{NE_IP_ADDRESS}}",
        "neType": "{{NE_TYPE}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Response

[
 {
   "category": "Temperature",
   "origin": "Chassis",
   "item": "n/a",
   "healthState": "Normal",
   "currentValue": "17  C",
   "minMaxValue": "17  C / 29  C",
   "rangeLimit": "-40 C / 65  C"
 }

Retrieve control plane configuration data from a node

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve information pertaining to control plane protocols from individual nodes. This includes information about:

  • RSVP-TE: enabled/disabled, and settings

  • LDP: enabled/disabled

  • ISIS routing instance: exists/does not, and properties

Retreiving this information is supported for the following nodes:

  • SAOS 6.x nodes

  • 6500

  • 8700

Use the Configuration Management/JOBS API to request this information:

SRLG management

SRLGs (Shared Risk Link Groups) and SRGs (Shared Risk Groups) enable calculation of diverse paths in the network.

SRLGs are used to identify common resources that can impact traffic for multiple services or multiple paths of the same service. Generally, SRLGs are limited to links (fibers that can be cut) but SRLGs can also apply to equipment related to the ports where the links terminate (for example, pluggable modules and line modules).

SRGs are generally used to model risks in other equipment, including: shelves, power supplies, and equipment groups (add/drop banks, ROADM degrees, and muxponder card sets).

Ciena uses SRLG as a general term that includes SRLGs and SRGs.

While conventions for SRLG usage can vary, it is common to model SRLGs using physical plant attributes. Of particular interest are the conduits that carry multiple fibers as they are very long, they are often buried, and they are subject to damage from construction. One SRLG can be used to represent a set of conduits and equipment (for example, an AMP chain) where all services traverse all components in that section of the plant (no add/drop points). Using this convention, Navigator MC would acquire the SRLGs associated with OTS topology, OMS topology, ROADM lines, line modules or ports.

'Groups of links with the same risk' versus 'A single link with a set of risks'

The technical definition of an SRLG is "a set of links affected by a common risk". Each risk has a set of affected links but a link could exist in many groups.

At Ciena, we associate risks (or groups of risks) that we call SRLGs (or bundle ids) to a single link. Each link has one set of risks and each risk (or group of risks) can be assigned to many links.

This section includes the following topics:

  • Configurable SRLG format

  • SRLG inventory

  • SRLG manual assignment

  • SRLG auto-assignment

Configurable SRLG format

This section describes the configurable SRLG format.

This section includes the following topics:

  • SRLG format

  • Opaque versus structured SRLGs

  • Structured SRLG configurable format

SRLG format

SRLGs can use any format that includes numbers or strings of printable characters.

MPLS customers use SRLGs which are 32-bit numbers. These SRLGs are restrictive because they must signal the SLRGs around the network and we want to minimize signalling overhead.

Navigator MC (as an SDN controller) is not as restrictive. Navigator MC also accepts long alpha-numeric strings.

Opaque versus structured SRLGs

Opaque SRLGs are values that Navigator MC cannot interpret. These values are provided by you, the customer, and are used by Navigator MC (and/or in-skin controllers like MPLS or OSRP) to create diverse routes. Fully diverse routes have no SRLGs in common. Best Effort diverse routes have some form of minimal intersection. Without being able to interpret SRLGs, the Navigator MC calculation for best effort only minimizes the intersection by the number of SRLGs and not by the importance of individual SRLGs.

Structured SRLGs are made up of fields that provide additional semantics to the value, such as the type of resource that is described by the Subnetwork or RegionId, the riskType that associates a SRLG category, and a riskValue. These fields are then combined to create one SRLG value (by "or-ing" bits into a number or concatenating characters into a string).

Structured SRLG configurable format

The SRLG configurable format includes the following characteristics:

  • Navigator MC ships a default format with the installation.

  • The SRLG format is disabled by default.

  • To use the Manual and Auto-assignment features, you must enable the SRLG format.

  • Once the SRLG format is enabled, the format cannot be changed or disabled. A feature to force update of the SRLG format is available.

  • Navigator MC only allows one SRLG format per deployment.

  • Irrespective of the SRLG format, Navigator MC stores the SRLG internally as a decimal and pushes the same to the network.

  • Navigator MC supports the following fields in the Structured SRLG format:

    • "riskType"

    • "subNetwork"

    • "riskValue"

The SRLG configurable format includes the following configurable attributes:

  • SRLG format type (Opaque or Structured).

  • SRLG display format (Bit, Decimal, Hexadecimal or String - for Opaque format only).

  • Field display names (for example, "Subnetwork" can be named "Region").

  • The start position and length of each field.

The following fields are available to the structured SRLG:

  • The "riskType" of resource with which the SRLG is associated.

    • The riskType must be pre-defined for auto-assigned SRLGs.

    • Ensure that riskType names are unique.

    • Navigator MC does not validate riskType deletion even if the riskType is associated with a SRLG.

    • Navigator MC ships with the default riskType Mapping. Mapping definitions can be changed using the POST or DELETE nsi/srlgformat/formatmappings API to modify riskType mappings.

    Type Description Input Mode Type Value

    Conduit

    Fiber plant

    Manual entry

    1000

    Fiber management

    Captive Office internal equipment

    Manual entry

    Site

    Floor, Building

    Manual entry

    0000

    Power supply

    Breaker panel, equipment external to the node

    Manual entry

    Custom

    User defined

    Manual entry

    OMS link

    ROADM degree

    Auto-assigned

    0011

    OTU link

    OTUk, OTUCn (no supporting layer)

    Auto-assigned

    Packet link

    Ethernet (no supporting layer)

    Auto-assigned

    Add/drop bank

    CCMD16x12 (in general, access structure)

    Auto-assigned

    0010

    Line module

    OTN/Packet circuit pack with interfaces

    Auto-assigned

    0110

    Photonic node

    ROADM TID

    Auto-assigned

    0001

    OTN node

    Switching or Broadband

    Auto-assigned

    Packet node

    Switching, Blade-based or Chassis

    Auto-assigned

    0100

    Multiservice node

    TID

    Auto-assigned

    Shelf

    Auto-assigned

    OTN subsystem

    Auto-assigned

    Packet subsystem

    Equipment group (eMOTR)

    Auto-assigned

  • The "Subnetwork" or "Controller id" is the owner of the SRLG namespace and ensures that the SRLG identifiers are unique.

    • Subnetworks must be pre-defined for auto-assigned SRLGs.

    • Navigator MC does not have any default Subnetwork Mappings. Subnetwork mappings configuration can be changed using the POST or DELETE nsi/srlgformat/formatmappings API to modify Subnetwork mappings.

  • The "riskValue" is the unique number assigned to the risk.

    • This may, or may not, be the current resource. For example, the SRLG could be stored on an OMS link but represent an amplifier node.

    • The SRLGs need to be unique to be effective, but the riskValue portion of the format must only be unique in the context of the other fields ("riskType" and "Subnetwork").

Assignable entity configurations

Navigator MC maintains an entity map for use with the auto-assignment feature.

You are provided with configuration control to allow filtering on Entity (fre, equipment or networkConstruct) with which you can enable auto-assignment. You can manage multiple entity filter criteria for a given entity type. An example is provided below which identifies various equipment types that can be marked as auto-assignable.

The filtering capabilities map to the inventory search capability supported by Navigator MC using the following APIs:

  • /nsi/api/search/equipment

  • /nsi/api/search/fres

  • /nsi/api/search/networkConstructs

  • /nsi/api/search/tpes

The filtering criteria must match the supported query parameter criteria in the APIs above (SearchField and SearchText are not supported).
The required filter criteria must be a first level attribute of an entityType.

Example of equipment filter criteria

In this example, the criteria is a name/value pair. The name field maps to one of the Search Inventory Query parameters for the corresponding Entity type. You must ensure that the provisionedSpec.partNumber is a query parameter supported by Navigator MC API /nsi/api/search/equipment.

{
      "id": "1",
      "type": "assignableEntityConfiguration",
      "attributes": {
        "entityType": "equipments",
        "filters": [
          {
            "riskType": "Add/Drop Bank",
            "criteria": [
              {
                "name": "provisionedSpec.partNumber",
                "values": [
                  "NTK723AA",
                  "NTK720CA"
                ]
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "riskType": "Line Module",
            "criteria": [
              {
                "name": "provisionedSpec.partNumber",
                "values": [
                  "NTK762MA"
                ]
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "riskType": "ROADM Degree",
            "criteria": [
              {
                "name": "provisionedSpec.partNumber",
                "values": [
                  "NTK722AA"
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
