Patch format user guidelines

The following user guidelines apply for patch format:

  1. Once an SRLG Format is enabled, it cannot be changed unless you include the following attribute in the patch body:

 "forceUpdate": true

  1. Updating an existing SrlgFormat is discouraged as it may render interpretation of existing SRLGs in the system corrupted and hamper auto-assignment functionality. Updating the previously used format must be changed in consultation with a Ciena specialist.

  2. The safe updates on SrlgFormat once the format is configured are:

    1. Updating Structure displayName

    2. Updating auto-assignment behavior

    3. Updating propagation behavior

    4. Adding new risk Type mappings

    5. Adding new subnetwork mappings

Enable/Disable SRLG Auto-assignment

To toggle SRLG auto-assignment behavior, use the SRLGFormat API for auto-assignment.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgformat/srlgAutoAssignment

A sample request is provided below.

Toggle Auto-assignment Behavior

true
Enable/Disable SRLG Propagation

To toggle SRLG propagation behavior, use the SRLGFormat API for propagation.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgformat/srlgPropagation

A sample request is provided below.

Toggle Propagation Behavior

true
Configure Navigator MC for multiple subnetworks

Configuring Navigator MC for multiple subnetworks consists of two steps.

Step 1: Define Subnetwork Mapping (required for Manual assignments, Auto-assignment and querying srlg in Structured format)

To create new Subnetwork mappings, use the SRLGFormat API for format mappings:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgformat/srlgFormatMappings

Sample request:

A response code of 200 indicates that the request succeeded. Upon creating the mappings, these will start appearing as part of the GET nsi/srlgformat and GET nsi/srlgformat/srlgFormatMappings response.

A sample request body to create mappings is provided below.

{
  "data": [
    {
      "type": "subNetwork",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "WestRegion",
        "value": "2"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "subNetwork",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "NewSubnetwork2Region",
        "value": "13"
      }
    }
  ]
}

To delete any obsolete Subnetwork mapping, use the SRLGFormat API for format mappings:

DELETE {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgformat/srlgFormatMappings

Sample request:

A response code of 200 indicates that the request succeeded. Upon deleting the mappings, the changes will start reflecting as part of the GET nsi/srlgformat and GET nsi/srlgformat/srlgFormatMappings response.

A sample request body to delete mappings is provided below.

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "subNetwork::NewSubnetwork2Region",
      "type": "subNetwork"
    },
    {
      "id": "subNetwork::NewSubnetwork1Region",
      "type": "subNetwork"
    }
  ]
}
Use the delete Subnetwork mappings with caution. Subnetwork mappings are used to interpret the SRLG applied in system. If any such mapping is deleted, it may result in errors while querying SRLG information entities with “include srlg” and may result in errors while triggering auto-assignment of SRLGs.

Step 2: Define Subnetwork Mapping (required for Auto-assignment)

For auto-assignment to work, the system considers the subnetwork tagged to the parent networkConstruct and gets the value of the tag from subnetworkMapping. You must tag the NetworkConstruct with the Subnetwork tag either through the Network Constructs API or the User Interface (UI).

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/api/v3/networkConstructs/{id}

Sample request:

{
  "operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "attributes": {
        "tags": [
          "EastRegion"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}

ConfigManagement: Align Config management with the new SRLG Format

Shareable SRLG is used with FB profile. There are two ways to provide SRLG values:

  1. SRLG value with REST input

  2. Autofill of SRLG value

SRLG value with REST input

You can provide SRLG values using an Navigator MC-defined format. The Navigator MC-defined format can be structured or opaque. It can be decimal. SRLG values are validated against the Navigator MC-predfined format and transformed into decimal values. Transformed decimal values will be invoked in the CLI SRLG value.

Autofill of SRLG value

Two attributes are defined in the REST input to autofill shareable srlg values. Nodal SRLG values will be retrieved from Navigator MC when isShareSrlgNodeAutofill or isShareSrlgLinkAutofill is true. Nodal SRLG values are applied on the NE and invoked in CLI SRLG value.

  1. Node value attribute: isShareSrlgNodeAutofill

  2. Link value attribute: isShareSrlgLinkAutofill

REST

Use the following API to create FB profile:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Request payload

  • FB profile creation - SRLG REST input

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "fbProfileConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
               "shelf":"1",
               "group":"41",
               "data": [
                {
                   "attributes":{
                         "action": "create",
                         "profileName":"fb_test",
                         "shareSrlgNode": {
                              "srlgStructuredValues": [
                                {
                                  "riskType": "Line Module",
                                  "Region": "mumbai",
                                  "riskValue": "1234"
                                },
                                {
                                  "riskType": "Line Module",
                                  "Region": "kolkata",
                                  "riskValue": "4567"
                                }
                              ]
                            },
                         "shareSrlgLink": {
                              "srlgStructuredValues": [
                                {
                                  "riskType": "Line Module",
                                  "Region": "mumbai",
                                  "riskValue": "1234"
                                },
                                {
                                  "riskType": "Line Module",
                                  "Region": "kolkata",
                                  "riskValue": "4567"
                                }
                              ],
                              "srlgValues": ["1223421", "11223453"]
                            },
                         "remoteNEName": "65TS_37"
                    }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
    },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "65TS_07",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "65TS_07"

      }
    }
  ]
}

  • FB profile creation - SRLG Autofill

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "fbProfileConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
               "shelf":"1",
               "group":"41",
               "data": [
                {
                   "attributes":{
                       "action": "create",
                       "profileName":"fb_test",
                       "remoteNEName":"65TS_071",
                       "isShareSrlgNodeAutofill":true,
                       "isShareSrlgLinkAutofill":true
                    }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
    },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "65TS_07",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "65TS_07"
      }
    }
  ]
}
BPO-IFD: Align Config management with the new SRLG Format

The SRLG format defined at BPO-IFD must be aligned to the SRLG format defined in NSI. The following capabilities can be used to align these formats:

  • Patch SRLG format (srlgSchema): This API is used to define SRLG format in BPO-IFD config resource.

  • Patch SRLG Enums (srlgEnums): This API is used to define Enums in BPO-IFD config resource that will be used by getSRLG and UpdatedSRLG (add operation) APIs.

  • Patch SRLG view format (srlgOpaqueValueFormat): This API is used to define getSRLG output format in BPO-IFD config resource. Three formats are supported:

    • Hex (Default)

    • Binary

    • Decimal

      Ciena recommends using decimal format, as it must be kept in sync with the SRLG format stored at NSI SRLG format (refer to GET nsi/api/srlgfromat).

Use the following API to update SRLG format:

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

Sample request:

A sample request body to update SRLG structure is provided below.

  • Patch SRLG structure on IFD config resource

{
    "properties": {
        "configurationProperties": {
            "ifd.srlg.srlgSchema": {
                "value": "unused:3,Region:5,riskType:4,riskValue:20"
            }
        }
    }
}

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

Sample request:

A sample request body to update SRLG enums is provided below.

  • Patch SRLG Enums at IFD config resource

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.srlg.srlgEnums": {
        "value": "riskType:Site=0,Photonic Node=1,ROADM Degree=3,ROADM Add/Drop Bank=2,Line Module=6,Conduit=8;Region:WestRegion=2, NewSubnetwork2Region=13"
      }
    }
  }
}

PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

Sample request:

A sample request body to update SRLG opaque value format is provided below.

  • Patch output format at IFD config resource

{
  "properties": {
    "configurationProperties": {
      "ifd.srlg.srlgOpaqueValueFormat": {
        "value": "decimal"

      }
    }
  }
}

Once share SRLG structure is defined at BPO-IFD, the user can add update SRLG values using share SRLG APIs already defined in Configuring a shareable SRLG list on a node.

Below is an example of assigning share SRLG on BPO-IFD based on SRLG values received from NSI SRLG (refer to GET nsi/api/srlg) API.

Assigning Opaque value

Use the following API:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{MplsOperationContainerResourceId}/operations

You can copy the output of NSI SRLG (refer to GET nsi/api/srlg) as input to this API.

Below is a sample NSI SRLG (refer to GET nsi/api/srlg) which can be used to provide input to this API.

  • NSI Opaque output

{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "resourceId": "1462493d-6fd8-342d-871f-32074c7fabee::EQPT_1_11",
      "resourceType": "equipment",
      "srlgSet": [
        {
          "combined": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651585",
              "35651697"
            ]
          },
          "auto": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651585"
            ]
          },
          "manual": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651697"
            ]
          },
          "inherited": {
            "srlgValues": []
          },
          "propagated": {
            "srlgValues": []
          }
        },
        {
          "plannedStartDate": "2024-12-26T10:30:01.607413Z",
          "manual": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "18874602"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

A sample request body to update SRLG using opaque value format is provided below.

  • Assigning opaque value

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "{{SRLG_NE_NAME}}"
      },
      "operation": "add",
      "srlgValues": [
        {
            "srlgValue": "35651585"
        }
    ]
  }
}

Assigning structured value

Use the following API:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{MplsOperationContainerResourceId}/operations

You can copy the output of NSI SRLG (refer to GET nsi/api/srlg) as input to this API. Below is the sample NSI SRLG (refer to GET nsi/api/srlg) which will be used to provide input to this API.

  • Assigning structured value

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "{{SRLG_NE_NAME}}"
      },

SRLG inventory

Use the API requests in this section to retrieve information about SRLGs.

To enable storage of multiple SRLG types, the underlying storage requires change:

  • Manual SRLG: maps to the SRLG applied on the Entity instance using the REST API or UI and can be applied to planned time expectations.

  • Auto SRLG: maps to an auto-assigned SRLG on the entity instance.

  • Propagated SRLG: maps to SRLGs that are propagated on the entity from the entities in the hierarchy (for example, NC SRLG propagated to EQPT).

  • Combined SRLG: maps to the combined SRLG set that represents: Manual SRLG + Auto SRLG + Propagated SRLG.

  • Discovered SRLG: represents the SRLG reported from the resource adapter (RA).

This section includes the following topics:

  • Retrieve SRLGs assigned to equipment, nodes, links or services (FRE)

  • Return details about an auto-assigned SRLG

Retrieve SRLGs assigned to equipment, nodes, links or services (FRE)

To retrieve SRLGs assigned to equipment, nodes, links or services (FRE), use the SRLG API.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

The following parameters are available:

  • (mandatory) "resourceType": fres, networkConstructs, TPEs, or equipment

  • (mandatory) "resourceID": the identifier of the equipment, networkConstruct, fre or tpe

  • (optional) "isStructured": Y to specify that SRLG values are to be returned using Structured notation according to the configured SRLG format or N to specify that SRLG values are to be returned using opaque/native (computed SRLG) notation. Default = N (computed SRLG).

  • (optional) "srlgType": one of the following: auto, manual, inherited, combined, propagated and discovered to include/exclude the srlg category in response. The default response is to only return manual SRLGs.

  • (optional) "plannedStartTime": return SRLGs that are applied using the specified plannedStartTime.

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates that the request succeeded.

A sample response for equipment using an opaque SRLG format is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "resourceId": "1462493d-6fd8-342d-871f-32074c7fabee::EQPT_1_11",
      "resourceType": "equipment",
      "srlgSet": [
        {
          "combined": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651585",
              "35651697"
            ]
          },
          "auto": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651585"
            ]
          },
          "manual": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "35651697"
            ]
          },
          "inherited": {
            "srlgValues": []
          },
          "propagated": {
            "srlgValues": []
          }
        },
        {
          "plannedStartDate": "2024-12-26T10:30:01.607413Z",
          "manual": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "18874602"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

A sample response for equipment using a Structured SRLG format is provided below.

    "attributes": {
      "resourceId": "1462493d-6fd8-342d-871f-32074c7fabee::EQPT_1_11",

        {

Return details about an auto-assigned SRLG

You can see the assignment details of any SRLG value, such as which resources in Navigator MC inventory have the been assigned a given SRLG value.

Given an SRLG value, you can retrieve:

  • All the resources where SRLG is set to Auto/Manual/Propagated/Inherited.

  • All the TPEs where SRLG is set to Auto/Manual/Propagated/Inherited.

  • All the FREs where SRLG is set to Auto/Manual/Propagated/Inherited.

  • All the equipment where SRLG is set to Auto/Manual/Propagated/Inherited.

  • All the networkConstructs where SRLG is set to Auto/Manual/Propagated/Inherited.

You can also check based on assignmentType of the SRLG, for example:

  • All the resources where SRLG is set to Auto.

  • All the TPEs where SRLG is set to Auto.

  • All the FREs where SRLG is set to Auto.

  • All the equipment where SRLG is set to Auto.

  • All the networkConstructs where SRLG is set to Auto.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/{srlgValue}/assignmentDetails

Sample response:

A sample response is provided below for SRLG value 39845896, and srlgType=auto.

{
  "data": {
    "assignmentDetails": {
      "auto": {
        "assignedResources": [
          {
            "resourceType": "networkConstructs",
            "resourceIds": []
          },
          {
            "resourceType": "equipment",
            "resourceIds": []
          },
          {
            "resourceType": "fres",
            "resourceIds": []
          },
          {
            "resourceType": "tpes",
            "resourceIds": [
              "fb41f041-1402-39ff-a6b5-47b162573d24::TPE_1_FTP_IPDATA_ipCtrl_7_3"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

SRLG manual assignment

To manually assign SRLGs, use the SRLG API.

Elements of the call

As part of the call, specify values for the following attributes:

  • "resourceId"

  • "resourceType": (FREs, networkConstructs, or equipment)

  • "srlgSet": an object comprising "plannedStartDate" and the manual SRLG object.

    The date format is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSSZ. Multiple SRLG sets can be specified for different "plannedStartDate"(s) and one set without "plannedStartDate" can be specified. SRLG values can be supplied either as opaque values using "srlgValues" or as structured SRLG values using "srlgStructuredValues".

For Navigator MC to understand the structured SRLG, the SRLG Format must be enabled and configured and the Structured SRLGs must comply with the SRLG Format. If the SRLG Format is configured as structured, SRLG values provided in opaque notation can be computed back to a Structured SRLG. Otherwise, the request is not accepted and validation errors are generated.

Sample request:

PUT {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

{
  "data": {
    "attributes": {
      "resourceId": "2000925292613460342",
      "resourceType": "fres",
      "srlgSet": [
        {
          "manual": {
            "srlgStructuredValues": [
              {
                "subNetwork": "NewYorkRegion",
                "riskType": "Conduit",
                "riskValue": 80023
              }
            ]
          }
        },
        {
          "plannedStartDate": "2018-09-26T10:30:01.607413Z",
          "manual": {
            "srlgValues": [
              "59520495"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

A response code of 200 indicates that the SRLG is updated.

SRLG auto-assignment

This section includes the following topics:

  • SRLG auto-assignment to resources

  • Clear SRLG auto-assignment from resources

SRLG auto-assignment to resources

To add SRLG auto-assignment to resources, use the SRLG API.

The following considerations apply to this operation:

  • Navigator MC is configured to apply auto-assignment (in the SRLG Format isAutoAssignment is set to True).

  • Auto-assignment is an asynchronous operation and you can query the job status to determine the status of the operation.

  • To auto-assign SRLGs in Navigator MC-managed resources, you must make separate requests for each EntityType (networkConstructs, equipments and TPEs).

  • Navigator MC only allows one auto-assignment, clear auto-assignment, propagation, or write to network operation to be running at any given moment.

  • Navigator MC will consider the entities that qualify for the filter criteria defined in "assignableEntityConfigurations" of the SRLG Format.

  • Navigator MC will skip those entities where the SRLGs are already auto-applied.

  • Navigator MC will automatically select the subnetwork/Controller identifier from the parent networkConstruct. A prerequisite is to tag the networkConstruct (Network Element) with a subnetwork and ensure that the subnetworkMapping is defined using the GCS mapping described in Configure Navigator MC for multiple subnetworks.

  • If Navigator MC is not able to compute the SRLG automatically for an entity instance, Navigator MC will mark the auto-assignment failed for that entity and will move to the next entity.

  • If Navigator MC is restarted, the auto-assigned values will be retained.

  • There will be separate pools on the basis of entity domain to manage uniqueness of the SRLG. The uniqueness index for the SRLG Format will be subnetwork+riskType.

  • The auto-assigned SRLG values will be unique to a specified pool.

You can trigger auto-assignment to resources maintained in the Navigator MC inventory as follows:

  • All applicable resources of a specified type (equipments, networkConstructs, TPEs, FREs) in the entire network.

  • All applicable resources of a specified type and riskType (for example, Add/Drop Bank).

The default entity instance filter and considerations for auto-assignment are as follows:

  • equipment:

    • ADD-DROP Bank: equipment where cardType is PEC: NTK723AA or NTK720CA

    • Line Module: equipment where circuitPack is NTK762MA, NTK762EA or NTK761AA (T-series only)

    • ROADM Degree: cardType: RLA PEC (to be filled by CI) is NTK722AA

  • networkConstructs:

    • Photonic Node: networkConstructs where memberFunction is ROADM. Only assigned to the primary shelf.

  • FREs: none

  • TPEs: none

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

A response code of 202 indicates that the request is accepted and will be processed in the background.

A sample request is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "op": "auto_assign",
    "attributes": {
      "resourceType": "equipment"
    }
  }
}

Auto-assignment is an asynchronous response. The success response returns a job identifier. The job status for the job can be accessed using the following API:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/job/{jobId}/details

Clear SRLG auto-assignment from resources

To clear SRLG auto-assignment from resources, use the SRLG API.

You can trigger a "clear auto-assignment" to resources maintained in the Navigator MC inventory as follows:

  • All applicable resources of a specific type (equipments, networkConstructs, TPEs, and FREs) in the entire network.

  • All applicable resources of a specific type and riskType (for example, Add/Drop Bank).

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

A response code of 202 indicates that the request succeeded.

A sample request is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "op": "clear_auto_assign",
    "attributes": {
      "resourceType": "equipment"
    }
  }
}

Navigator MC will allow only one auto-assign, clear auto-assign, propagation, or write-to-network operation to be running at any given moment.

Clear Auto-assignment is an asynchronous response. The success response returns a job identifier. The job status for the job can be accessed using the following API:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/job/{jobId}/details

SRLG Propagation

Once Auto-assignment and desired manual assignment of SRLG on resources is completed, you can proceed to trigger SRLG propagation of the SRLGs of all underlying entities to IP Link and IP interfaces.

You can trigger propagation in the following ways:

  • Given IP Link and corresponding interfaces. Input required: resourceType=fres and resourceId={fried}

  • All IP Links and corresponding interfaces on a single networkConstruct. Input required: resourceType=networkConstructs and resourceId={ncId}

  • All IP Links and corresponding interfaces on the entire network. Input should not provide resourceType and resourceId.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

A response code of 202 indicates that the request succeeded.

A sample request is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "op": "propagate",
    "attributes": {
     "resourceType": "fres",
     "resourceId": "3382882828724"
    }
  }
}

Navigator MC will allow only one auto-assign, clear auto-assign, propagation, or write-to-network operation to be running at any given moment.

Propagation is an asynchronous response. The success response returns a job identifier. The job status for the job can be accessed using the following API: GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/job/{jobId}/details

Propagation will consider the following entities:

  • All IP links that belong to 6500 Network Elements.

  • A networkConstruct’s SRLG will be propagated to Fre only in case the Fre is a cross-connect within the Network element.

SRLG Propagation view:

Propagation will apply and persist (in Navigator MC) the propagated SRLG on the following entities:

  • IP Links

  • IP interface on either side of IP Link

View of persisted propagated SRLGs post propagation:

Following propagation, Navigator MC will mark the interfaces as srlgMismatch if the interface’s calculated SRLG is different than discovered SRLG.

SRLG Write to Network

Once SRLG assignment (Manual/Auto/Propagate) on resources maintained in Navigator MC inventories is completd, you might want to realize the assigned SRLGs on the nodes (write SRLGs to Nodal entities).

You can trigger the write-to-network operation in the following ways:

  • Given IP interface. Input required: resourceType=tpes and resourceId={tpeId}

  • All IP interfaces on a single networkConstruct. Input required: resourceType=networkConstructs and resourceId={ncId}

  • All IP interfaces on the entire network. Input should not provide resourceType and resourceId.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg

A response code of 202 indicates that the request succeeded.

A sample request is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "op": "write_to_network",
    "attributes": {
     "resourceType": "tpes",
      "resourceId": "1519f4e7-25c6-3d5f-b35f-57e3549cc5c7::TPE_2_FTP_IPDATA_ipCtrl_7_3"
    }
  }
}

Navigator MC will allow only one auto-assign, clear auto-assign, propagation or write-to-network operation to be running at any given moment.

Write to Network is an asynchronous response. The success response returns a job identifier. The job status for the job can be accessed using the following API:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/job/{jobId}/details

SRLG Mismatch API

You might want to know of any discrepencies of SRLGs in the Navigator MC and the network. This might help you to decide if SRLGs need to be pushed down to the network.

A REST API call has been provided to facilitate this operation. Currently, only IP interfaces are considered to have write of SRLG capabilities. So the API response provides only IP interfaces where SRLG mismatch is being seen.

Sample request:

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/srlgMismatch

Sample response:

A sample response is provided below.

{
  "data": [

Retrieve SRLG operations status

You might need to see the operation status of SRLG operation performed. To retrieve the SRLG operations status, use the SRLG API.

At least one query parameter is mandatory.

  • "jobId": job id provided as response of POST call

  • "jobStatus": in_progress/completed/failed/partially_completed

  • "jobType": auto_assign/clear_auto_assign/propagate/write_to_network

The job status always returns the last triggered operation status.

Sample request:

GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/ifd/api/v2/srlg/job/status

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates that the request succeeded.

A sample response is provided below.

{
  "lastTriggeredTime": "2019-07-01T15:44:40.775Z",
  "id": "44542b46-b919-416a-a7cf-fd59283e4706",
  "srlgJobType": "write_to_network",
  "jobParams": {},
  "jobDetails": [],
  "srlgJobStatus": "in_progress"
}

Validate SRLG values

You might need to validate SRLG values prior to manually assigning them to any resource. To validate the SRLG values, use the SRLG API.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgFormat/srlg/validate

Sample request (native)

{
  "data": {
    "srlgValues": ["1223421", "11223453"]
  }
}

Sample request (structured)

{
  "data": {
    "srlgStructuredValues": [
      {
        "riskType": "Line Module",
        "Region": "Subentwork1",
        "riskValue": "1234"
      },
      {
        "riskType": "Line Module",
        "Region": "Subentwork2",
        "riskValue": "4567"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Sample response:

A response code of 200 indicates that the validation succeeded.

Transform SRLG value (Structure <→ Opaque)

You might need to convert an opaque SRLG value to structured SRLG value or vice versa. To transform the SRLG value, use the SRLG API.

At least one query parameter is mandatory.

POST {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/nsi/api/srlgFormat/srlg/transform

Sample request:

A sample request is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "srlgValues": ["1223421", "11223453"]
  }
}

Sample response:

A sample response is provided below.

{
  "data": {
    "srlgStructuredValues": [
      {
        "riskType": "Line Module",
        "Region": "Subentwork1",
        "riskValue": "1234"
      },
      {
        "riskType": "Line Module",
        "Region": "Subentwork2",
        "riskValue": "4567"
      }
    ],
    "srlgValues": ["1223421", "11223453"]
  }
}
Upgrade impacts

There are two upgrade workflows:

  1. Upgrade from 3.6. EA2-5 or earlier to 3.6-xxx

  2. Upgrade from 3.6. EA2-7 to later to 3.6-xxx

Structural changes were introeduced to SrlgFormat. So, for any system with upgrade path with:

  • Option 1: the system will preserve the SRLG values, but will reset the SlgFormat to default. The user will have to re-configure the SrlgFormat.

  • Option 2: System will preserve the SRLG values as well as the previously configured SRLG format.

Create the Facility Bypass Profile

You can use the Navigator MC API to create a facility bypass (FB) profile at the NE level.

The NE allows the creation of multiple FB profiles in the system which can then be attached to an IP interface. You can create the facility bypass profile on the following Network elements:

  • 6500-T and 6500-PTS (Release 13.0)

  • 6x MPLS capable node 6.17.1

To create an FB profile on the Network element, execute the following CLI command:

mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile create auto-fb-profile <auto-fb-profile-name string >

{

        [bandwidth-percentage-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

         bandwidth-percentage-value <NUMBER: 0...100>]

          [setup-hold-priority-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

          setup-hold-priority-value <NUMBER: 0...7>]

          [link-preference <yes | no>]

          [affinity-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

              < color-group-include-all <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> |

                  color-group-include-any <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> |

                  color-group-exclude-any <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> >]

                [srlg-mode < maximal | strict | none>]

}

Attributes:

Action Attributes Type Values Description

create

profileName

string

bandwidthPercentageSource

string

User fast-reroute-object

bandwidthPercentageValue

integer

0 - 100

linkPreference

string

Yes
No

affinitySource

string

user fast-reroute-object

affinityDisjoint

string

Yes
No

setupHoldPrioritySource

string

user fast-reroute-object

setupHoldPriorityValue

0 - 7

srlgMode

string

maximal strict none ignore

colourGroupIncludeAny

string

colourGroupIncludeAll

string

colourGroupExcludeAny

string

Create/Edit the Facility Bypass Profile using shareable SRLG

You can use the Navigator MC API to create or edit a Facility Bypass (FB) profile at the NE level with the shareable SRLG list.

You must manually provide the shareable SRLG, or the SRLG automatically fills in based on the NE shareable SRLG if it exists.

You can also provide the optional property of "remoteNode" to allow Navigator MC to automatically set the linkBypassSRLG based on that information.

You can also allow Navigator MC to auto-assign shareable SRLGs.

To create a FB profile with SRLG values on the Network element, execute the CLI command:

mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile create auto-fb-profile fb_profile bandwidth-percentage-source user bandwidth-percentage-value 50 setup-hold-priority-source user link-preference no affinity-source user affinity-disjoint no srlg-mode maximal share-srlg-link 434110950,434110951 share-srlg-node 434110947,434110948,434110949\n

To unset the FB profile with SRLG values on the Network element, execute the CLI command:

mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile unset auto-fb-profile fb_test_affinity bandwidth-percentage-source bandwidth-percentage-value setup-hold-priority-source link-preference affinity-source affinity-disjoint srlg-mode share-srlg-link share-srlg-node\n

Attributes:

Create FB profile

Action: Create
Attributes: remoteNEName, shareSrlgNode, shareSrlgLink
Type: string, list, list
Values: none, none, none
Description: none, List contains node SRLG values, List contains link SRLG values

Update/Set FB profile

Action: Set
Attributes: remoteNEName, shareSrlgNode, shareSrlgLink
Type: string, list, list
Values: none, none, none
Description: none, List contains node SRLG values, List contains link SRLG values

Unset FB profile

Action: Set
Attributes: shareSrlgNode, shareSrlgLink
Type: none, none
Values: none, none
Description: List contains node SRLG values, List contains link SRLG values

Edit the Facility Bypass Profile

You can use the Navigator MC API to edit a Facility Bypass (FB) profile, which is used to change some network properties.

  • 6500-T and 6500-PTS (Release 13.0)

  • 6x MPLS capable node 6.17.1

To edit an FB profile on a network element, execute the following CLI command:

mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile set fb-profile <auto-fb-profile-name string>

{

  [bandwidth-percentage-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

  bandwidth-percentage-value <NUMBER: 1...100>]

 [setup-hold-priority-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

  setup-hold-priority-value <NUMBER: 0...7>]

 [link-preference <yes | no>]

 [affinity-source <user | fast-reroute-object>

  < color-group-include-all <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> |

    color-group-include-any <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> |

    color-group-exclude-any <MPLS TE Admin Color Group> >]

 [srlg-mode < maximal | strict | none>]

 [force-apply]

}
mpls tunnel-auto-fb-profile unset fb-profile <auto-fb-profile-name string (1...31)>

{

 [bandwidth-percentage-source

  bandwidth-percentage-value

 [setup-hold-priority-source

  setup-hold-priority-value]

 [affinity-source

  < color-group-include-all  |

    color-group-include-any  |

    color-group-exclude-any> ]

 [srlg-mode]

 [link-preference]

}

Set/Unset the Facility Bypass Profile to an IP interface

You can use the Navigator MC API to set or unset a Facility Bypass (FB) profile to an individual IP interface at the NE level for the following network elements:

  • 6500-T and 6500-PTS (Release 13.0)

  • 6x MPLS capable node 6.17.1

To set facility bypass profile to an ip interface on the Network element, execute the following CLI command:

mpls traffic-eng set ip-interface <interfaceName> frr-auto-fb-profile <AutoFbProfile>

To unset facility bypass profile to an ip interface on the Network element, execute the following CLI command:

mpls traffic-eng unset ip-interface < interfaceName > frr-auto-fb-profile

Attributes:

Set facility bypass profile to an ip interface

Action: update
Attributes: interfaceName, frrAutoFbProfile
Type: string. string
Values: none, none
Description: none, none

Unset facility bypass profile to an ip interface

Action: Unset
Attributes: interfaceName
Type: string
Values: none
Description: none

Configuring a shareable SRLG list on a node

You can se the Navigator MC REST API to assign a set of shareable Shared Risk Link Group (SRLG) values to node supporting packet services and infrastructure. This information can then be taken into account when using strict SRLG routing of dynamic MPLS corouted tunnels and unidirectional Facility Bypass (FB) tunnels.

The list of SRLG values is optional and is entered to allow Navigator MC to automatically identify SRLG values that are permitted to be shared when creating co-routed tunnels, FB profiles, or FB tunnels. This shareable SRLG is not propagated/stored to the node level and is stored only at Navigator MC level.

For example, the shareable SRLG value can allow you to identify the ROADM risk that has has to be shared between primary and backup even during strict SRLG diversity.

Navigator MC will automatically detect the SRLG values being used if they are configured on the node, and will use these for any protected, dynamic corouted MPLS tunnel with strict/mandatory diversity constraints.

The SRLG value will follow the 32-bit-based mapping the operator defines instead of being a flat 32 bit integer value.

The set of shareable or permitted SRLG values is managed as a list, and so the Navigator MC REST API allows you to:

  • set all initial values for the list

  • add new values to the list

  • remove values from the list

  • reset the list so that it is empty

You can also use the API to query a node and retrieve the data presently contained in the list.

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Preparing for the operation

  • Retrieving the current SRLG list

  • Replacing values in the current SRLG list

  • Adding values to the SRLG list

  • Removing values from the SRLG list

  • Deleting all values from the SRLG list

Preparing for the operation

The API calls used to work with SRLG values on a node use a "workflow operations" model. To issue the API calls required to interact with the SRLG lists on nodes, you must first obtain a 'MplsOperationContainer' resource ID:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources?exactTypeId=ifd.v2.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer

This call will produce a response resembling the following:

{
    "items": [
        {
            "id": "5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89",
            "label": "Resource for ifd.v5.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer",
            "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v5.resourceTypes.MplsOperationContainer",
            "productId": "5ad8c341-3dd4-4b8b-86c9-951c969a8884",
            "tenantId": "78bb407f-1023-4b89-a615-a4b569a00b77",
            "shared": false,
            "properties": {},
            "discovered": false,
            "differences": [],
            "desiredOrchState": "active",
            "orchState": "active",
            "reason": "",
            "tags": {},
            "providerData": {
                "templateResources": {}
            },
            "updatedAt": "2018-04-19T16:27:05.982Z",
            "createdAt": "2018-04-19T16:27:05.766Z",
            "autoClean": false
        },
...

The required ID is shown in the "id" field of the returned object.

You can then use this ID to issue a REST API query to start any of the SRLG operations. This is done with a call resembling:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/

The call will include a JSON body particular to each type of operation, as described later.

All SRLG operations are Asynchronous. To verify whether the ongoing operation is complete, and whether it was successful or not, you must issue GET requests using the operation ID returned by the starting request:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{RID}/operations/{OID}

where RID is the OperationContainer resource ID and OID is the Operations ID returned by the operation request.

The 'state' field of that reply indicates if the operation is complete and 'successful' or 'failed'. If supported, the response will also provide the replied data (e.g. SRLG value list) in the 'outputs' field (as indicated below)

For example this call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89/operations/5ad8c3a8-0be1-469b-968a-e19925887f0a

where "5ad8c3a8-0be1-469b-968a-e19925887f0a" is the Resource and Operations IDs from previous GET/POST request, will produce a response like the one shown below.

{
    "id": "5ad8c3a8-0be1-469b-968a-e19925887f0a",
    "resourceId": "5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89",
    "interface": "getPermittedNodalSrlg",
    "inputs": {
        "networkElement": {
            "name": "3930_MCP_4"
        }
    },
    "outputs": {
        "srlgValues": [
            {
                "srlgRiskSummary": 0,
                "srlgValue": "0x04400017",
                "srlgRegionId": 1,
                "srlgRiskValue": 23,
                "srlgRiskType": "ROADM Node"
            }
        ]
    },
    "state": "successful",
    "reason": "",
    "progress": [],
    "providerData": {},
    "createdAt": "2018-04-19T16:28:24.547Z",
    "updatedAt": "2018-04-19T16:28:25.041Z",
    "resourceStateConstraints": {},
    "executionGroup": "lifecycle"
}

In the return example above, note the following:

  • "srlgValues":

    • this signifies the beginning of the SRLG values associated with the target node, in object format

  • "srlgValue": "0x04400017"

    • the full numerical value is provided along with the broken-down fields

  • "srlgRiskType": "ROADM Node"

    • note the enum-name translation of the numerical value

  • "state": "successful",

    • must ensure the state is successfull, if executing, must poll anew

When initiating an IFD Operation, a JSON-structured body is given with two fields;

  • "interface" names the operation to be performed

  • "inputs" is a structure whose fields provide the parameters to the operation

The values of those fields depend on the operation to be performed.

Retrieving the current SRLG list

The IFD operation (interface) to retrieve the current Permitted Nodal SRLG values for a given node is 'getPermittedNodalSrlg'.

The provided input is one field, "networkElement", with one sub-field "name: that identifies the target node.

The successful reply ('outputs') also contains one field, "srlgValues", which is a list of SRLG objects as shown in earlier examples (for example [ {'srlgRiskType': 'ROADM Node', …​}, …​ ] ).

If no SRLG values are present, or if the values cannot be retrieved for any reason, an empty list is returned. If values are present, the individual elements of the list will provide all the fields interpreted from the SRLG value by the schema, as well as the 'srlgValue' field with the numerical form of the value.

For example, a call to retrieve the current set of SRLG values stored on a node would resemble the following:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89/operations

where "5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89" is a Resource ID obtained from a previous GET request, would include the following:

{
  "interface": "getPermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
    "networkElement": {
        "name": "3930_MCP_4"
    }
  }
}

This would result in a response resembling the following:

{
    "id": "5ad8c6aa-803e-42bf-a8aa-fedb6e5a8ec1",
    "resourceId": "5ad8c359-63a0-4d51-85d3-790bcd500a89",
    "interface": "getNodalSrlg",
    "inputs": {
        "networkElement": {
            "name": "3930_MCP_4"
        }
    },
    "outputs": {},
    "state": "requested",
    "reason": "",
    "progress": [],
    "providerData": {},
    "createdAt": "2018-04-19T16:41:14.288Z",
    "updatedAt": "2018-04-19T16:41:14.288Z",
    "resourceStateConstraints": {},
    "executionGroup": "lifecycle"
}

Replacing values in the current SRLG list

The IFD operation (interface) to update the current Permitted Nodal SRLG values for a given node is 'updatePermittedNodalSrlg'.

The provided input has three fields:

  • "networkElement"/"name", the target node identified by name

  • "operation", is 'add', 'remove', 'replace', or 'delete'

  • "srglValues", is a list of SRLG objects (same as for the get), not needed for 'delete'

For the 'replace' action, the list of given SRLG values included in the call will replace the list of SRLG values current stored on the target node. If the list on the node contains no values, then these values simply populate the list.

For example:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d/operations

where 5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d is theResource ID from previous GET request, would include the following:

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
            "name": "3930_MCP_4"
      },
      "operation": "replace",
      "srlgValues": [
        {
            "srlgRiskSummary": 0,
            "srlgRegionId": 1,
            "srlgRiskValue": 255,
            "srlgRiskType": "ROADM Node"
        }
    ]
  }
}

This response to this call would resemble the following:

{
    "id": "5ad8e3d2-d779-41ab-be35-dc44f4e53eb8",
    "resourceId": "5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d",
    "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
    "inputs": {
        "networkElement": {
            "name": "3930_MCP_4"
        },

                "srlgRiskSummary": 0,
                "srlgRegionId": 1,

Adding values to the SRLG list

For the 'add' action, the specified values are added to those already in the SRLG list on the node (if any). For example, the following call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d/operations

where 5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d/ is the Resource ID from a previous GET request, would include the following:

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
          "name": "3930_MCP_4"
      },
      "operation": "add",
      "srlgValues": [
        {
            "srlgRiskSummary": 0,
            "srlgRegionId": 1,
            "srlgRiskValue": 22,

For example, the following call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d/operations

in which 5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d is the Resource ID from previous GET request, would include the following:

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
        "name": "3930_MCP_4"
      },
      "operation": "remove",
      "srlgValues": [

                "srlgRiskSummary": 0,
                "srlgRegionId": 1,

Deleting all values from the SRLG list

For the 'delete' action, no "srlgValues" is included in the input and all current SRLG values associated with the target node are removed.

For example, the following call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d/operations

in which 5ad8e33d-ca63-4830-b677-ca7d918bcb2d is the Resource ID from previous GET request, would include the following:

{
  "interface": "updatePermittedNodalSrlg",
  "inputs": {
      "networkElement": {
          "name": "3930_MCP_4"
      },
      "operation": "delete"
  }
}

This call would produce a response that resembles the following:

{

Configure Traffic Engineering (TE) parameters for an IP interface

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to configure Traffic Engineering parameters for an IP interface, including:

  • SRLG

  • Link Cost

  • Link Cost

  • Affinity values

The MPLS control plane can use these properties when computing optimal network paths.

This topic includes the following sections:

  • SRLG Attributes

  • Updating an SRLG value

  • Updating multiple SRLG values

  • Updating SRLG value ranges

  • Un-setting an SRLG value

  • Adding an SRLG value

  • Removing an SRLG value

SRLG Attributes

When setting SRLG values, the API call uses the following attributes:

Action Attributes Type Values Description

update

srlValues

List

contains SRLG values

srlgRegionId

integer

srlgRiskType

integer

srlgRiskSummary

integer

srlgRiskValue

integer

linkCost

integer

resourceColorGroupName

string

isSrlgValuesRange

boolean

True False

unset

srlValues

List

contains SRLG values

linkCost

integer

resourceColorGroupName

string

add/remove

srlValues

List

contains SRLG values

srlgRegionId

integer

srlgRiskType

integer

srlgRiskSummary

integer

srlgRiskValue

integer

isSrlgValuesRange

boolean

True False

These values in an API call body, together with values for link cost, and affinity, would resemble the following example:

"srlgValues":[
    {
        "srlgRegionId": 6,
        "srlgRiskType": 7,
        "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
        "srlgRiskValue": 483
    },
],
"linkCost": 200,
"interfaceName": "if",
"resourceColorGroupName": "tdm_color_gr"

Updating an SRLG value

A request to update an SRLG value would include a body resembling the following:

Sample request payload

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "ipInterfaceConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "update",
                    "srlgValues":[
                        {
                            "srlgRegionId": 6,
                            "srlgRiskType": 7,
                            "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
                            "srlgRiskValue": 483
                        }
                    ],
                    "linkCost": 200,
                    "interfaceName": "if",
                    "resourceColorGroupName": "tdm_color_gr"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "relationships": {
      "networkConstructs": {
        "data": [
          {
            "type": "networkConstructs",
            "id": "{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}",
      "type": "networkElement",
      "attributes": {
        "ncId": "{MANAGEMENT_SESSION_ID}",
        "neName": "{NE_NAME}",
        "ipAddress": "{NE_IP_ADDRESS}",
        "neType": "{NE_TYPE}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Updating multiple SRLG values

A request to update multiple SRLG values would include a body resembling the following:

Sample request payload

{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",

      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "ipInterfaceConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
              "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "update",
                    "srlgValues":[
                        {
                            "srlgRegionId": 6,
                            "srlgRiskType": 7,
                            "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
                            "srlgRiskValue": 483
                        },
                        {
                            "srlgRegionId": 6,
                            "srlgRiskType": 7,
                            "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
                            "srlgRiskValue": 484
                        },
                        {
                            "srlgRegionId": 6,
                            "srlgRiskType": 7,
                            "srlgRiskSummary": 1,
                            "srlgRiskValue": 485

Place a network element into or out of maintenance mode

You can use the Navigator MC API to place a network element into, or out of, maintenance mode. This can be helpful when a troubled node is generating excessive events or alarms, as these will cease once the network element is in Maintenance Mode. Once the issue is resolved you can take the node out of Maintenance Mode, which will cause the node to be rediscovered and resynchronized.

There are two related operations that you can invoke with this API call: "inMaintenance" and "outMaintenance". Each will change the connectivity state of a specific node’s ManagementSession:

  • inMaintenance: if the ManagementSession is currently in a CONNECTED/COMPLETED discoveryState, this operation will initiate the process to put the network element into a Loss of Association (LOA) state, and will disconnect the Resource Adapter (RA) session.

  • outMaintenance: if the ManagementSession is currently in a FAILED state (with the Fail Reason as "Under Maintenance"), this operation will re-initiate the enrollment process to reconnect and resynchronize the network element.

This action uses the following API calls:

Retrieving the SessionID

The first step in managing a network element’s Maintenance Mode is to retrieve that network element’s sessionId. You do this a a GET operation using the following call:

GET/discovery/api/v4/managementSessions

The API returns the list of management sessions and their Connection state.

Setting the Maintenance Mode

Once you have identified the sessionId of the target network element, use that value as part of the following API call:

PATCH/discovery/api/v4/managementSessions/{sessionId}

  • A device that has a connection state of COMPLETED/CONNECTED can be placed inMaintenance.

  • A device that has a connection state of PENDING and a ‘failureReason’ as ‘Under Maintenance’ can be placed outMaintenance.

In each case, the body of the API call will include an operation specifier resembling the following:

{
 "operations" : [
 {
 "op": "{operationName}"
 }]
}

For example:

{
 "operations" : [
 {
 "op": "inMaintenance"
 }]
}

The API response will resemble the following:

{
  "data": {
    "id": "0a13aa66-8d13-449d-8675-29ceb1574a30",
    "type": "managementSessions",
    "attributes": {

Simplified port configuration

Navigator MC supports a simplified port configuration process using the REST API. Using this API call, and working in conjunction with pre-existing port configuration templates and mapping files, you can provide only basic port configuration inputs including the NE name, port location, and a few additional parameters.

Based on this information Navigator MC will determine which port configuration template to apply, execute that port configuration template, wait for a period of time, and then resynchronize the NE. For a port deconfiguration, upon completion of the port deletion on the NE, Navigator MC will resynchronize the NE so it can learn of the changes made.

A file containing the necessary configuration data is available separately for each type of card that can be used with the supported NEs. Additional configuration files for new cards can be loaded, when required, using a separate API call.

A separate set of mapping files specifies which traffic rates are supported by each type of pluggable equipment. This file can be updated as required using the API.

Note: When multiple rates are available, Navigator MC will always apply the highest supported rate on a port. For example, if a mapping file specifies that pluggable X supports both ETH40GPKT and ETH10GPKT, Navigator MC will always apply ETH40GPKT rate on the port.

This capability is currently supported for the following NEs:

  • 6500-T series Release 13.0 and later

  • 6500-S PTS Release 13.0 and later

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Provisioning a port

  • Deprovisioning a port

  • Deprovisioning Rollback on a port

  • Loading a new configuration file

  • Viewing all currently loaded PEC definitions

  • Downloading a PEC definition file

  • Deleting a PEC definition file

  • Adding pluggable rate mappings

  • Obtaining a list of mapping files

  • Downloading a mapping file

  • Deleting a mapping file

  • Sample JSON for PEC

  • Sample pec code format portTextVsSpeed

  • Sample pec code format allowedValues

  • Sample Mapping File

  • Sample TL1 Script

Provisioning a port

The User should manually resync the NE on Navigator MC, if the Port is modified(create/delete entity) via Site Manager or any different source.

Provision a port using the followng API call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/provision

Sample Request Payload

{
  "name": "{{NE_NAME}}",
  "shelf": "{{SHELF}}",
  "slot": "{{SLOT}}",
  "port": "{{PORT}}",
  "otn": "false",
  "maxFrameSize": "9000",
  "rate": "ETH40GPKT",
  "description": "test",
  "reSyncInventory": false,
  "scriptFileProperties": {
     "linkflap": "1",
     "shaper-compensation": 28
  },
  "portFlapDampeningInput": {
      "state": "enable",
      "suppressLimit": "2000",
      "reuseLimit": "1000",
      "halfLife": "5",
      "maxSupressTime": "20"
  },
  "mplsSpeculativeHash": "on"
}

The full supported request payload is shown below. Not all parameters supported in the payload are required for all port configurations. This full payload includes some parameters which are assigned default values (and so must only be included if you need to use different values):

  • clientType: Default value is "ETH"

  • reSynchInventory: Default value is "false"

  • otn: This flag is used to specify which rate should be applied on the port. If true then Optical Transport Network (OTN) rate will be applied on port; otherwise ETHERNET rates will be applied on the port.

  • rate: Specifies the rate to be applied on port. When the otn parameter is "true", this is OTUn. When the OTN parameter is set to false, then the rate will default to the configuration in the PecCode.json file. For PTS devices, it will be defaulted to ETH<allowedValue>G/M, and for 6500T devices it will be defaulted to ETH<allowedValue>PKT.

  • scriptFileProperties: Use only if you want to override or add to the parameters passed to scriptFiles for execution.

  • portFlapDampeningInput: Use only if you want to add port flap dampening on the port.

  • mplsSpeculativeHash: Use it to configure MPLS speculative hash on the port. Valid values are on and off with the default value as off.

Below is the table for portFlapDampeningInput parameters validation and default values:-

Parameter Valid Value Default Value

state

enable/disable

disable

suppressLimit

1-20000

2000

reuseLimit

1-20000

1000

halfLife

1-30

5

maxSupressTime

1-20000

20
Full request payload
{
"name": "string",
"shelf": "string",
"slot": "string",
"port": "string",
"clientType": "string",
"otn": false,
"maxFrameSize": "string",
"description": "string",
"rate": "string",
"customerId": "string",
"scriptFileProperties":
"additionalProp1": "string",
"additionalProp2": "string",
"additionalProp3": "string"
"portFlapDampeningInput":
      "state": "string",
      "suppressLimit": "string",
      "reuseLimit": "string",
      "halfLife": "string",
      "maxSupressTime": "string"
"mplsSpeculativeHash": "off", // default off
"reSyncInventory": false //default false
}

Deprovisioning a port

The User should manually resync the NE on Navigator MC, if the Port is modified(create/delete entity) via Site Manager or any different source.

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/deProvision

Sample Request Payload
{
  "name": "SIM1",
  "shelf": "1",
  "slot": "9",
  "port": "1",
  "otn": false,
}

Deprovisioning Rollback on a port

Port-Deprovision REST API provides rollback capabilities in the event of provisioning failure so they do not have remnants of configuration left of a device which then require manual clean-up or which could then cause issues if a clean-up delete operation was exercised.

  • The Port Deprovision native REST API checks if a port is already out-of-service (OOS-MA) and if so skips the command to put the port out-of-service.

  • The Port Deprovision native REST API upon a device command failure (e.g. due to 'child' resource still existing) ensures the port is returned to its original state. If the port was originally in-service then upon a device command failure, the Port Deprovision REST API rolls back the port state to in-service as it would have changed the state to out-of-service. If the port was originally out-of-service then upon a device command failure, Navigator MC leaves the port in the out-of-service state.

Loading a new PEC definition file

Provided you have the unique Product Equipment Code (PEC) for a card, you can load a new PEC definition file which can then be used when configuring ports for that card. The definition file for a card will be named <PEC>.json.

You can load a PEC definition file using the following Configuration Management API call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/pecs

The payload included in the call will be sent as multipart content, and will contain fileDetails, the Uploaded File and PEC code as name.

For example, to load the file for a card with PEC NTK614AA, the payload would resemble the following:

Sample payload
------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="NTK614AA.json"
Content-Type: application/json


------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="name"

NTK614AA
------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG--

This will produce a response resembling the following:

Sample response*
{
    "id":"1d5a1548-93f8-43bd-982e-1b4a157bc400",
    "type":"pec",
    "attributes":
        {
            "name":"NTK614AA1"
        }
}

Downloading a PEC definition file

You can use the API to download a specific PEC definition file. Use the following Configuration Management API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/pecs/<id>

In response, Navigator MC will download the file.

Deleting a PEC definition file

You can use the API to delete a specific PEC definition file. Use the following Configuration Management API call:

Delete {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/pecs/<id>

Navigator MC will return the response code 204.

Adding pluggable rate mappings

In addition to the unique configuration file for each card, Navigator MC uses a set of mapping files to identify the connection rates supported on different pluggable equpiment (storing different values for each combination of "pluggable type" + "pluggable PEC").

To upload a new mapping file, use the following API call:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/mappings

The payload for this call should be sent as multipart content, and will contain fileDetails, Uploaded File and name. This name should be the same name that is mentioned in the pecCode definition file.

Sample Request Payload

------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="pktotnMapping.json"
Content-Type: application/json


------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="name"

pktornMapping
------WebKitFormBoundaryaS7AFtS4wvl8B3iG--

Sample Response

{
  "id": "e581e628-a44e-4c06-abb9-9e0ef29d87ce",
  "type": "mapping",
  "attributes": {
    "name": "pktotnMapping"
  }
}

Obtaining a list of pluggable rate mappings

You can use the API to obtain a list of all pluggable rate mappings currently uploaded to Navigator MC. Use the following Configuration Management API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/mappings

Sample Response

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "2fa31ef6-5854-4e24-9db6-b4263396a84c",
      "type": "mappings",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "mroMapping"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "e581e628-a44e-4c06-abb9-9e0ef29d87ce",
      "type": "mappings",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "pktotnMapping"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Downloading a mapping file

You can use the API to download a specific PEC definition. Use the following Configuration Management API call:

GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/mappings/<id>

In response, Navigator MC will download the file.

Deleting a mapping file

You can use the API to delete a specific mapping file. Use the following Configuration Management API call:

Delete {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/port/mappings/<id>

Navigator MC will return the response code 204.

Sample JSON for PEC

{
    "id": "NTK762EA",
    "type": "6500T",
    "operationScriptFiles": [
      {
        "operationType": "PROVISION",
        "scriptFiles": [
            {
                "commandType": "tl1",
                "commandFile": "Create_PTP"
            },
            {
                "commandType": "cli",
                "commandFilesBySpeed": {
                    "ETH10GPKT": "Set_10G_NNI_Port_Params_ETH",
                    "ETH40GPKT": "Set_40G_NNI_Port_Params_ETH",
                    "ETH100GPKT": "Set_100G_NNI_Port_Params_ETH"
                }
            }
        ],
        "otnScriptFiles": [
            {
                "commandType": "tl1",
                "commandFile": "Create_OTN_PTP"
            },
            {
                "commandType": "cli",
                "commandFilesBySpeed": {
                    "OTU2": "Set_10G_NNI_Port_Params_OTN",
                    "OTU2E": "Set_10G_NNI_Port_Params_OTN",
                    "OTU3": "Set_40G_NNI_Port_Params_OTN",
                    "OTU4": "Set_100G_NNI_Port_Params_OTN"
                }
            }
        ]
      },
      {
        "operationType": "DE-PROVISION",
        "scriptFiles": [
          {
            "commandType": "tl1",
            "commandFile": "Delete_PTP"
          }
        ],
        "otnScriptFiles": [
          {
            "commandType": "tl1",
            "commandFile": "Delete_OTN_PTP"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "mappingFile": "pktotnMapping"
}

The mappingFile contains rate details. A sample format is given below. Other ways to provide rate information is by using the "portTextVsSpeed" or "allowedSpeedValues" tag.

Sample PEC code format portTextVsSpeed

{
    "id": "NTK614AA",
    "type": "PTS",
    "operationScriptFiles": [
      {
        "operationType": "PROVISION",
        "scriptFiles": [

Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) overview

The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is an inter-Autonomous System routing protocol.

The primary function of a BGP speaking system is to exchange network reachability information with other BGP systems. This network reachability information includes the list of Autonomous Systems (ASes) that the reachability information traverses. This information is sufficient for constructing a graph of AS connectivity for this reachability, from which routing loops may be pruned and, at the AS level, some policy decisions may be enforced.

BGP uses TCP as its transport protocol. This eliminates the need to implement explicit update fragmentation, retransmission, acknowledgement, and sequencing. BGP listens on TCP port 179. The error notification mechanism used in BGP assumes that TCP supports a "graceful" close (i.e., that all outstanding data will be delivered before the connection is closed). A TCP connection is formed between two systems. They exchange messages to open and confirm the connection parameters. KEEPALIVE messages may be sent periodically to ensure that the connection is live. NOTIFICATION messages are sent in response to errors or special conditions. If a connection encounters an error condition, a NOTIFICATION message is sent and the connection is closed.

Definition of Commonly Used Terms

  • Autonomous System (AS): The classic definition of an Autonomous System is a set of routers under a single technical administration, using an interior gateway protocol (IGP) and common metrics to determine how to route packets within the AS, and using an inter-AS routing protocol to determine how to route packets to other ASes. Since this classic definition was developed, it has become common for a single AS to use several IGPs and, sometimes, several sets of metrics within an AS. The use of the term Autonomous System stresses the fact that, even when multiple IGPs and metrics are used, the administration of an AS appears to other ASes to have a single coherent interior routing plan, and presents a consistent picture of the destinations that are reachable through it.

  • BGP Identifier: A 4-octet unsigned integer that indicates the BGP Identifier of the sender of BGP messages. A given BGP speaker sets the value of its BGP Identifier to an IP address assigned to that BGP speaker. The value of the BGP Identifier is determined upon startup and is the same for every local interface and BGP peer.

  • BGP speaker: A router that implements BGP.

  • EBGP: External BGP (BGP connection between external peers).

  • External peer: Peer that is in a different Autonomous System than the local system.

  • IBGP: Internal BGP (BGP connection between internal peers).

  • Internal peer: Peer that is in the same Autonomous System as the local system.

  • IGP: Interior Gateway Protocol - a routing protocol used to exchange routing information among routers within a single Autonomous System.

  • FSM: Finite state machine maintained by BGP for each peer.

Retrieving a BGP configuration from a node

To retrieve BGP configuration data from a node, make a GET request that inclues the NE name as a parameter using the following API call:

  • GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/bgpconfiguration/{neName}

For example:

GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/bgpconfiguration/65TS_0119

This will produce a response resembling the following:

Provisioning BGP: Loopback or IP interface

You can use the Navigator MC API to create, edit, and delete a BGP session between a pair of BGP enabled nodes. Navigator MC supports these actions for a BGP session between the control plane Loopback of the nodes, and where the enabled nodes are targeted at specific IP interface.

The API calls used for these actions are:

  • POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions for creating and editing a BGP session

  • DELETE: /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions for deleting a BGP session

Note: Creating or editing a BGP session will also selectively resynchronize the node with Navigator MC. Deleting the BGP session will completely resynchronize the node with Navigator MC.

Supported devices

Navigator MC supports the provisioning of BGP sessions for the following equipment:

  • 6500 T-series (software version 13.0+)

  • 6500 PTS (software version 13.0+)

  • 3926 (software version 6.18+)

Configuring BGP sessions using IP interface as destination

Navigator MC supports BGP provisioning with an IP interface destination, encompassing the following scenarios:

  • iBGP sessions are between AGN and AN node

  • iBGP session are between directly connected nodes (at IP level)

  • iBGP sessions are set towards an explicit IP interface (not a loopback)

  • a BGP session will be created in both directions (from AN to AGN and from AGN to AN), where AN is acting as RR client to AGN.

  • you can choose to enable BGP IP BFD; it will be enabled by default.

    • BGP will automatically create BFD session when reachability is established

The example below shows the provisioning of a BGP session between two nodes (one acting as the "a" end and other other as the "z" end) using the IP interface address. This uses the following Navigator MC API call, together with the payload shown in the example:

  • POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions

For details about supported parameters for this call, see API inputs for BGP create/edit.

BGP session created with interface ip, when interface_ip is taken as REST input
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEA",
        "ipInterface":"41.0.0.2"
     },
     "zEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEB",
        "ipInterface":"41.0.0.1"
     }
    }
  ]
}

Configuring BGP sessions at Loopback level

Where some AGN nodes are configured as Route Reflectors (RR), network deployment can use a hierarchy of RRs for which AGN nodes are clients, rather than fully mesh all AGNs nodes with iBGP sessions. Instead, BGP sessions can be created between the following:

  • between AGN and RR (in a client/server relationship)

  • between RR pair (to create a mesh)

Note 1: The iBGP session will be created in both directions.

Note 2: These iBGP sessions can be configured between AGNs that have same AS number.

The examples below show the provisioning of a BGP session between two nodes (one acting as the "a" end and other other as the "z" end) using the Loopback IP address. These use the following Navigator MC API call, together with the payload shown in each example:

  • POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions

For details about supported parameters for this call, see API inputs for BGP create/edit.

A BGP session created with loopback ip, when management_ip is taken as REST input
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC",
      }
    }
  ]
}
A BGP session created with loopback ip and one end is rrEnabled
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC",
        "rrEnabled": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
A BGP session created with loopback ip and addressFamily passed in REST input
{
  "data": [
    {
      "addressFamilies":[
          "unicast"
      ],
      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC"
      }
    }
  ]
}
A BGP session created with loopback ip and bfdMonitor passed in REST input
{
  "data": [
    {
      "bfdMonitor": "mhop",
      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC"
      }
    }
  ]
}
A BGP session created with loopback ip and description passed in REST input
{
  "data": [
    {
      "description": "test-indra",
      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC"
      }
    }
  ]
}
A BGP session with loopback ip and authentication password passed in REST input
{
  "data": [
    {

      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEA",
        "authenticationPassword": "indra"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB",
         "authenticationPassword": "nil"

      "grEnabled": false,

Editing a BGP session

You can edit a BGP session using the following API call:

POST : /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions

Sample request payload
{
  "data": [
    {
      "action": "update",
      "addressFamilies":[
          "unicast"
      ],
      "bfdMonitor": "mhop",
      "description": "test",
      "grEnabled": false,
      "keepaliveTime": 10,
      "holdTime": 20,
      "advertisementInterval": 30,
      "aEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB",
        "prefixList":{
            "type": "prefix-list",
            "direction": "out"
        },
        "orf":{
            "enabled": "false",
            "type": "prefix-list",
            "direction": "tx"
        },
        "routeMap":{
            "type": "toAN_Map",
            "direction": "out"
        }
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEC",
        "authenticationPassword": "ciena"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Deleting a BGP session

You can delete a BGP session, whether using a Loopback IP or IP interface, using the following API call:

DELETE : /configmgmt/api/v1/bgpsessions

Example for Loopback IP:
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEA"
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "neName": "G4658-1-NEB"
      }
    }
  ]
}
Example for IP interface:
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEA",
        "ipInterface":"41.0.0.2"
     },
     "zEnd": {
       "neName": "G4658-1-NEB",
        "ipInterface":"41.0.0.1"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Notes on inputs:

  • Both-ended and Single-ended BGP session: BGP session can be supported on both ends or just a single end.

    • For a both-ended session, the mandatory input will be NE_NAME/NE_IP for the local and peer node.

    • For a single-ended BGP session, the mandatory input will be peer ip and peer as numbers.

    • For each end(aend and zend), if separate description("description") is provided then, each end is provisioned with separate description. If only one description is provided, then both the ends are provisioned with same description.

"aEnd": {
        "neName": "NE_NAME",
