        }
      }

  • updateSourceInterfaceName will be executed for a BGP session on a Loopback IP.

  • Address family: This parameter can have the values "unicast" or "labeled-unicast". The Address family value will be used for all of the following attributes, which are expected to have the same value:

    • nbrActivates,

    • orf,

    • nextHopSelfs

    By default, these values will be "unicast" or "labeled-unicast". If an input is provided for any of the above attributes, the provided value(s) will override the default value(s).

  • NE default value: If no input is provided for these values, then no values will be inserted. Navigator MC will, however, use NE default values for the following attributes.

    • keepaliveTime

    • holdTime

    • advertisementInterval

  • shelf and group:

    • If input is provided: User input shelf group value will be used.

    • If input is not provided:

    • Single shelf configuration: shelf group value will be retrieved from NSI.

      • TIDC/Multishelf configuration: Not supported.

GCS attributes for BGP session

Retrieving an inventory of route reflector configurations on a node

The term "route reflection" describes the operation of a BGP speaker that advertises an iBGP learned route to another iBGP peer. Such a BGP speaker is said to be a "route reflector" (RR), and such a route is said to be a reflected route.

You can use the Navigator MC API to see whether a node has been set up as route reflector (RR) and, if so, view the route reflector configuration. This can help to drive the iBGP session creation between RRs, and between RR and AGN nodes.

To identify nodes configured as RRs, Navigator MC uses the Inventory Search API call to look for nodes for which the following attribute is set to True:

  • rrConfigured

Note: BGP-capable nodes are by default RR-enabled and this cannot currently be altered. For this reason, as soon as an AS is created, bgpPackage and rrConfig will be reported and the RR capability of the node cannot be disabled. However, the ClientToClient property can be toggled between Enabled and Disabled for intraCluster. When an AS is created, the node will have clusterId and clientToClient enabled by default, and these can be used for intraCluster route reflection.

Retrieve an inventory of iBGP or eBGP sessions

You can use the Navigator MC API to retrieve an inventory of iBGP or eBGP sessions in the managed network. This can aid you in seeing the BGP peer topology, and whether certain nodes are configured as BGP peers.

From an inventory perspective, Navigator MC treats iBGP session like as a form of topological link representing the bidirectional BGP peer connectivity. Since iBGP session are between nodes, a node will appear to be connected to multiple iBGP peers.

The following are key properties of an iBGP session:

  • Local Node (in terms of Node as well as its router ID): Loopback IP

  • Remote Peer (in term of Node as well as its router ID): Loopback IP

  • admin/operational state

Filter or search for BGP (iBGP/eBGP) sessions

The Navigator MC Inventory Search API call (/nsi/api/search/fres) supports searching a FRE on the basis of single NetworkConstruct in InventorySearch. This endpoint can be used to search for BGP (iBGP and eBGP) sessions starting/ending on a specific node.

Navigator MC’s API allows you to:

  • Retrieve and view an inventory of iBGP sessions and clearly identify session properties.

    iBGP inventory information includes, depending on availability from the supporting node:

    • local and remote nodes

    • applicable configuration details

    • state

  • Filter iBGP sessions:

    • starting / ending on a specific node

  • Retrieve / view inventory of eBGP sessions and clearly identify its properties.

    eBGP inventory information includes, depending on availability from the supporting node:

    • remote node / interface

    • applicable configuration details

    • state

  • Filter eBGP sessions:

    • starting / ending on a specific node

Searches for BGP sessions add particular filters to the existing search API (/nsi/api/search/fres), for example:

Search for entities with service class "BGP session":

GET {{BP SERVER}}/nsi/api/search/fres?resourceState=planned,discovered,plannedAndDiscovered&serviceClass=BGP Session&limit=30

Search for entnties with signalContentType BGPSESSION:

GET {{BP SERVER}}/nsi/api/search/fres?resourceState=planned,discovered,plannedAndDiscovered&signalContentType=BGPSESSION&limit=30

Search for entities with LayerRate BGP:

GET {{BP SERVER}}/nsi/api/search/fres?resourceState=planned,discovered,plannedAndDiscovered&layerRate=BGP&limit=30

Search for entities with a specific NetworkConstructID:

GET {{BP SERVER}}/nsi/api/search/fres?resourceState=planned,discovered,plannedAndDiscovered&networkConstruct.id=23a2b5a2-e3ce-3872-a832-77439d61f4f1&limit=30

BGP Session TPE?s can be filtered to show those that conform to a particular attribute. For example, the response below might be returned for the following filter:

searchText=internal&searchFields=data.attributes.layerTermina tions.bgpPackage.peerType

Note: Here the inclusion of "internal" filters for iBGP session CTPs; "external" would instead search for eBGP session CTPs.

BGP session: Ciena proprietary traps support

MCP 3.6 introduces the support of the following two Ciena proprietary traps:

  • cienaCesBgpPeerInEstState, and

  • cienaCesBgpPeerOutEstState

The behavior related to these two traps is in line with the BGP session management (inventory) feature as follows:

  1. Inventory: Inventory dynamic update with the following behavior:

    1. cienaCesBgpPeerInEstState: When Navigator MC receives this trap from a managed NE, then the latest inventory of the BGP peer (TPE) is retrieved from the NE and Navigator MC is updated. If the peer information is not yet present in Navigator MC, then it is created or else it is updated with the latest inventory retrieved at the time. When the peer has moved into the Established state, the latest information will then also include adjacency information, which is required to stitch the BGP session (FRE), even in those scenarios where the update-source is not done for the BGP neighbor. This includes the AN-AGN BGP session over the interface IPs.

    1. cienaCesBgpPeerOutEstState: When Navigator MC receives this trap from a managed NE, then Navigator MC patches the operationalState of the BGP peer (TPE) as down. Other information is not updated. As a result, if the BGP session (FRE) is already stitched and present in Navigator MC, then its operationState will also transition to "Out of Service". The latest information is not retrieved from the network upon receiving this event because doing so would unstitch the BGP session FRE from Navigator MC. The BGP session operationState transitions to "Out of Service" on this trap, which indicates a potential issue with the BGP session in the network; the user can now initiate the required corrective actions.

  2. Alarm: The cienaCesBgpPeerOutEstState will raise an Alarm with severity Major as coming in a trap. The cienaCesBgpPeerInEstState will clear the alarm. For details related to alarms, see Alarm management

  3. Alarm correlation: Alarm-to-service correlation, that is, the raised alarm is correlated to the BGP session. For related details, see the following:

    • "Query Layer 2 alarm to service correlation" in Correlation engine, and/or

    • "Query Layer 2 services affected by an alarm identifier and related counts" in Alarm management

Note: BGP session support is through REST API only. The correlated BGP session for the raised alarm cannot be opened in the Navigator MC UI.

Retrieve details for BGP tunnels in the network

You can use the Navigator MC API to retreive details regarding BGP tunnels in the network, including:

  • An inventory of BGP tunnels

  • Route details for BGP tunnels

Note the following significant aspects of this capability:

  • This is an on-demand data retrival. The nodes involved will not be resynchronized as part of this request; so the data returned will be based on information collected during the most recent synchronization.

  • This request will treat the Primary path as the Active path in all cases.

  • All users who have access to packet infrastructure queries will have sufficient permissions to discover BGP tunnels.

  • If any errors are encountered while requesting the active or configured path, the errors will be included in the response and a "Partial" flag will be set to True to indicate that the returned data is incomplete.

The Navigator MC API currently supports discovery of BGP tunnels on the following devices:

  • 6500 T-series, Release 13.05

  • 6500 PTS, Release 13.05

  • 3926m with SAOS 6.18

Note 1: Currently the capability to retrieve this data is limited to the API; it is not yet supported in the Navigator MC UI.

Note 2: The API retrieves the set of nodes between A and Z nodes provided that a) the BGP tunnels use Loopback IP addresses and b) all Loopback IP addresses use the /32 subnet.

Note 3: A request for the BGP tunnel inventory between two nodes will fail if another BGP tunnel retrieval between the same nodes is already underway.

Note 4: With enhanced APIs you will be able to fetch BGP Tunnel using following methods:

  • Node Names at both ends

  • Loopback IP for zEnd (MSE handoff scenario)

  • PW FRE (Intra Metro)

  • PW CTP (MSE PW handoff)

This topic includes the following sections:

  • BGP details request and response parameters

  • Retrieving a list of BGP tunnels between two nodes

  • Retrieving a list of BGP tunnels between two nodes, plus their configuration details

  • Retrieving active route details for BGP tunnels

BGP details request and response parameters

The API call to retrieve the BGP inventory uses the following structure:

  • BGP inventory request structure

BGP inventory request structure using Node name at both ends
{
  "productId": "Async Task PID",
  "label": "Get BGP Tunnel Data",
  "properties": {
    "operationName": "getBGPTunnelInfo",
    "input": {
      "aEnd": {
        "ncName": "",
        "location": {
          "shelf": "",
          "eqptGrp": ""
        }
      },
      "zEnd": {
        "ncName": "",
        "location": {
          "shelf": "",
          "eqptGrp": ""
        }
      },
      "direction": [
        "a_to_z","z_to_a"
      ],
      "route": [
        "active","configured"
      ]
    }
  }
}
BGP inventory request structure using Loopback IP for zEnd
{
  "productId": "Async Task PID",
  "label": "Get BGP Tunnel Data",
  "properties": {
    "operationName": "getBGPTunnelInfo",
    "input": {
      "aEnd": {
        "ncName": "",
        "location": {
          "shelf": "",
          "eqptGrp": ""
        }
      },
      "zEnd": {
	"loopbackIP": ""
      },
      "direction": [
        "a_to_z"
      ],
      "route": [
        "active","configured"
      ]
    }
  }
}

        "a_to_z","z_to_a"
      ],
      "route": [
        "active","configured"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Use NE fallback method for users/passwords if RADIUS unavailable

You can use the Navigator MC API to set and update the local user and password, either:

  • on a single NE

  • by bulk on a large set of NEs in case the user/password information needs to be updated on the entire network

If RADIUS is unavailable, you can use the fallback method as local authentication. Note the following requirements:

  • A unique user/password is required on each NE. This unique user/password must only be for the fallback scenario, where RADIUS authentication is not available.

    In this case, a unique user/password is created by Navigator MC on the NE.

  • In the fallback mode, the user needs to contact the NOC operator who verbally provides the current fallback password for the NE.

Use the Network element configuration API to perform the actions related to the fallback method listed in the following table. The actions to manage fallback users are captured in the "fallbackUsers v1" folder.

REST API Description

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers

View NE fallback user accounts information

POST /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers

Create one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

DELETE /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers

Delete one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/passwordPolicy

View global NE fallback user password generation policy

PATCH /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/passwordPolicy

Update one or more parameters of NE global fallback user password generation policy

POST /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords

Reset the password of one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords/schedules

View all NE fallback user password reset schedules

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords/schedules/{id}

View a specific NE fallback user password reset schedule

DELETE /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords/schedules/{id}

Delete a specific NE fallback user password reset schedule

View NE fallback user accounts information

Sample request:

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers

If no filter is used, all the fallback user accounts are returned in the response.

Sample response:

{
    "meta": {
        "total": 3
    },
    "data": [
        {
            "neType": "6500",
            "neName": "BV0132A",
             "username": "FALLBACK",
             "password": "H{63qF^_sr",
            "lastOperationState": "Succeeded",
            "lastOperationNote": "User creation: succeeded",
             "lastOperationTime": "2019-06-14T01:51:39.815Z"
        },
        {
            "neType": "6500",
            "neName": "BV0132B",
             "username": "FALLBACK",
             "password": "xa1gVav*6_ ",
            "lastOperationState": "Succeeded",
            "lastOperationNote": "User creation: succeeded",
             "lastOperationTime": "2019-06-14T01:51:39.829Z"
        },
        {
            "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
            "neName": "WS5_waveserver-18_3",
             "username": "FALLBACK",
             "password": "xA7gVav*6_ ",
            "lastOperationState": "Succeeded",
            "lastOperationNote": "User creation: succeeded",
             "lastOperationTime": "2023-07-20T10:25:39.829Z"
        }
    ]
}

To retrieve a subset of the full result, use the applicable filter:

  • "neNames": a list of comma-separated NE names.

  • "lastOperationState": supported values are "In-progress", "Succeeded", "Failed" and "System-restored".

  • "offset": the offset for the next page.

  • "limit": the page size; the default is 20.

Create one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

A global user name is used to create the fallback user account on all the 6500 or Waveserver NEs managed by an Navigator MC server.

The global user name is configurable. The default user name is "FALLBACK".

It is your responsibility to maintain the NE compliance if the global fallback user name needs to be customized.

Make sure that you customize the global user name before starting to create fallback user accounts on NEs.

If the global user name is changed after some fallback user accounts have already been created, it is possible to have more than one fallback user account created on an NE. It is user’s responsibility to clean up the old user account manually, if the fallback user account needs to be deleted.

Sample request:

POST /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers

To create the fallback user account on all managed 6500 NEs, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "6500". The input payload is as follows.

{
    "neType": "6500"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To create the fallback user account on a specified list of 6500 NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": ["BV0132A", "BV0132B"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [
        "BV0132A",
        "BV0132B"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

Waveserver devices can be of type Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5. Therefore Navigator MC users to pass the typegroup of the Waveserver devices i.e. CienaWaveserver in parameter "neType" to create fallback users on Waveserver family.

Individual neType values as Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5 are not supported.

To create the fallback user account on all managed Waveserver NEs, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "CienaWaveserver". The input payload is as follows.

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To create the fallback user account on a specified list of Waveserver NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": ["WS5_waveserver-18_3", "WS5_waveserver-18_5"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [
        "WS5_waveserver-18_3",
        "WS5_waveserver-18_5"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

Delete one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

To delete all the previously created fallback user accounts on 6500 devices, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "6500". The input payload follows.

{
    "neType": "6500"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To delete the fallback user account on a specified list of 6500 NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": ["BV0132A", "BV0132B"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [
        "BV0132A",
        "BV0132B"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

Waveserver devices can be of type Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5. Therefore Navigator MC users to pass the typegroup of the Waveserver devices i.e. CienaWaveserver in parameter "neType" to delete fallback users on Waveserver family.

Individual neType values as Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5 are not supported.

To delete all the previously created fallback user accounts on Waveserver devices, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "CienaWaveserver". The input payload follows.

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To delete the fallback user account on a specified list of Waveserver NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": ["WS5_waveserver-18_3", "WS5_waveserver-18_5"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [
        "WS5_waveserver-18_3",
        "WS5_waveserver-18_5"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

Deleting the fallback user directly from the device is not recommended.

Follow the below recovery procedure to delete the user from Navigator MC in case the fallback user gets deleted from the device directly:

  • Recreate the fallback user on the device. To create the fallback user, see Create one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs.

  • Delete the fallback user from Navigator MC. To delete the fallback user, see Delete one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs.

View global NE fallback user password generation policy

The default policy is generated when the system starts up. Random passwords are generated for the fallback user accounts based on the password generation policy.

Sample request:

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/passwordPolicy

Sample response:

{
    "data": {
        "lowercaseMinimum": 1,
        "uppercaseMinimum": 1,
        "digitMinimum": 1,
        "specialMinimum": 1,
         "passwordLength": 10,
         "maximumConsecutiveCharacters": 3
    }
}

Update one or more parameters of NE global fallback user password generation policy

The default password generation policy complies with the 6500 or Waveserver device complex password rules.

It is your responsibility to maintain the NE compliance if the password generation policy needs to be customized.

A sample request payload is as follows.

Sample request:

PATCH /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/passwordPolicy

{
    "lowercaseMinimum": 3,
    "passwordLength": 12
}

Sample response:

The response shows all the password generation policy parameters after the update. A sample response is as follows.

{
     "lowercaseMinimum": 3,
     "uppercaseMinimum": 1,
     "digitMinimum": 1,
     "specialMinimum": 1,
      "passwordLength": 12,
      "maximumConsecutiveCharacters": 3
}

Reset the password of one or more NE fallback user accounts on 6500 or Waveserver NEs

Sample request:

POST /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords

To reset the password on all the previously created fallback user accounts, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "6500". The input payload follows:

{
    "neType": "6500"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To reset the password of the fallback user account on a specified list of 6500 NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": ["BV0132A", "BV0132B"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [
        "BV0132A",
        "BV0132"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To schedule a recurring password reset job on a bulk or specified NE(s), specify the "resetSchedule" block with the "startTime" and "frequency" parameters specified. The supported frequency values are "daily" and "weekly", case insensitive. The valid date format to pass in the parameter "startTime" is "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ" and only UTC dates are supported. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "resetSchedule": {
        "frequency": "daily",
        "startTime": "2019-09-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "6500",
    "neNames": [],
    "resetSchedule": {
        "id": "795dab64-4afa-4ef3-9d04-19edbd55b062",
        "frequency": "DAILY",
        "neNames": [],
        "nextExecutionTime": "2019-09-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "state": "In-progress"
}

Waveserver devices can be of type Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5. Therefore Navigator MC users to pass the typegroup of the Waveserver devices i.e. CienaWaveserver in parameter "neType" to reset fallback user’s password on Waveserver family.

Individual neType values as Waveserver, Waveserver Ai and Waveserver 5 are not supported.

To reset the password on all the previously created fallback user accounts, specify the "neType" parameter only. The only supported value is "CienaWaveserver". The input payload follows:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver"
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To reset the password of the fallback user account on a specified list of 6500 NEs, specify both the "neType" parameter and the "neNames" parameter. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": ["WS5_waveserver-18_3", "WS5_waveserver-18_5"]
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [
        "WS5_waveserver-18_3",
        "WS5_waveserver-18_4"
    ],
    "state": "In-progress"
}

To schedule a recurring password reset job on a bulk or specified NE(s), specify the "resetSchedule" block with the "startTime" and "frequency" parameters specified. The supported frequency values are "daily" and "weekly", case insensitive. The valid date format to pass in the parameter "startTime" is "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ" and only UTC dates are supported. A sample input payload follows.

Sample request:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "resetSchedule": {
        "frequency": "daily",
        "startTime": "2023-07-20T00:00:00Z"
    }
}

Sample response:

{
    "neType": "CienaWaveserver",
    "neNames": [],
    "resetSchedule": {
        "id": "995dab64-4afa-4ef3-9d04-19edbd55b062",
        "frequency": "DAILY",
        "neNames": [],
        "nextExecutionTime": "2023-07-20T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "state": "In-progress"

View all NE fallback user password reset schedules

GET /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords/schedules

{
    "meta": {

DELETE /fallback-user-mgmt/api/v1/fallbackUsers/resetPasswords/schedules/{id}

Retrieve the span length of an OTDR trace

This capability estimates the length of the fiber by comparing the baseline and current files of LONG trace type. The resulting length is in meters (m). This is typically useful for the cases where there may be a fiber break situation for a span.

The pulse width and max fiber length of the CURRENT and BASELINE SOR files must be the same.

Navigator MC supports the retrieval of the OTDR span length for the following devices:

  • 6500 S-Series (12.1+)

The API call resembles the following:

curl -X GET "{{BP Server}} /otdr/api/v1/spanlength?session_id={{Device Mgmt Session Id}} &trace_id={{OTDR Entity}}" -H "accept: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer <code>"

This produces a system response resembling the following, the returned value is the Navigator MC estimated length of the span.

Sample response:

{
  "estimated_fiber_length": 55460.568909591226
}

Working with multi-hop IP BFD sessions

You can use the Navigator MC REST API to create or enable a multi-hop IP BFD session between iBGP peers in your network. This can be used to help detect BGP faults quickly, and trigger a BGP PIC (a protection switch at the BGP level).

You can also use the API to retrieve a list of all such multi-hop IP BFD sessions currently configured on a single node, or between two specific nodes.

Finally, you can use the API to delete an IP BFD session between two nodes.

This topic includes the following sections:

  • Creating or enabling a multihop IP BFD session

  • Retrieving details for a single IP BFD session

  • Deleting an IP BFD session

Creating or enabling a multihop IP BFD session

You can create a multi-hop (MHOP) BFD session between a pair of nodes by making an API call that explicitly identifies the two nodes and, optionally, la BFD profile. If you do not specify a profile, the NE will use a default profile.

In response, Navigator MC will then set up an MHOP BFD session on each node that points to the loopback of the remote peer in a mirrored configuration.

This capability is supported on the following devices:

  • 6500 T-Series 13.0, 13.05

  • 6500 PTS 13.0, 13.05

You can use the following Configuration Management API call to create an MHOP BFD session:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/mhopbfdsessions

Include the following parameters in the payload:

  • "source": the source node

  • "neighbour": the BFD neighbour node

"bf* dProfile": the BFD profile to use, if not the NE’s default profile

For example:

{"source"="NE1, "neighbour"="NE2", "bfdProfile": "Default-1"}

The Navigator MC response should be one of the following:

Success: HTTP response code 200 (ack/Success {No-content}).

Invalid request: HTTP response code 400

Failure: 500 Internal server error with the RA response embedded in the message.

Retrieving details for a single IP BFD session

You can also use the API to view a list of MHOP BFD sessions already created for an NE, and their administrative and operational states. You can also retrieve the more specific list of the sessions between two particular nodes.

You can use the following Configuration Management API call to retrieve a list of MHOP BFD sessions for a node or between two nodes:

GET {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/mhopbfdsessions

Include the "source" parameters as part of the payload to retreive the list of profiles on that node. Add the "neighbour" parameter to retrieve the list of sessions between the Source and Neighbor nodes.

Sample payload

{"source"="NE1, "neighbour"="NE2"}

Sample response - single-node request

Deleting an IP BFD session

You can use the following API call to delete a multi-hop IP BFD session:

{BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/mhopbfdsessions

As part of this call, you must provide:

  • The names of the source and neighbour NEs

  • The name of the session to be deleted

You should perform the operation to delete the session from both the NEs (the source and the neighbour) separately, to completely remove the session from both ends.

Sample Request Payload
Payload = {"source"="NE1, "neighbour"="NE2", "bfdSessionName": "test-session"}
Sample Response
Success case : Http response code 200 (ack/Success {No-content})
Failure case : 500 Internal server error with the RA response embedded in message.

Possible error response codes are:

  • 200: Delete BFD session request is executed.

  • 400: Invalid request

  • 500: Exception/error returned from RA

Setting a LAG queue

You can use Navigator MC’s API to configure default Queue settings for a logical ethernet port (LAG).

This custom setting can be called as part of LAG creation.

The Queue default settings for a LAG are the same as those for ethernet physical ports, where the Queue CIR/EIR is driven by the port Rate.

For a LAG, "rate" is based on its primary port rate * n (where n is number of primary ports). Navigator MC currently assumes that n=1 (so, you are configuring a single-member LAG).

Supported devices

Navigator MC supports this capability for the following devices:

  • 6500-T

  • 6500-PTS

  • 39xx (6x platform in general)

Note: For SAOS 6.x devices, the port speed must be set before configuring the LAG queue settings.

Pre-requisite

The GCS attribute 'autoLAGSettings' governs whether queue settings are permitted.

The default value is "False". LAG queue settings will be enabled when value is true.

Supporting scripts

Navigator MC requires specific scripts to configure a LAG port’s queue settings. Some scripts are pre-loaded for 6500 devices:

Table 28. 6500 script support
LAG rate Script name

1 Gbps

Set_1G_LAG_Port_Params_ETH

10 Gbps

Set_10G_LAG_Port_Params_ETH

40 Gbps

Set_40G_LAG_Port_Params_ETH

100 Gbps

Set_100G_LAG_Port_Params_ETH

For SAOS 6.x devices, this capability is available only when the corresponding 6.x custom scripts have been uploaded. Custom scripts can be uploaded using Navigator MC’s Custom Script feature.

API call and examples

Use Navigator MC’s JOB POST REST API of the Network Element Configuration to invoke requests:

POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Asynchronous notification after completion of the job will be available against the JOB_ID.

The examples below illustrate queue setting when creating LAG port on 6500 and SAOS 6.x devices respectively.

Creating a LAG on a 6500 device
{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "lagConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
                "shelf":"1",
                "group":"9",
                "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "create",
                    "aggName":"ag",
                    "primaryPorts": "1/1",
                    "ethernetSettings": true
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}
Creating a LAG on a SAOS 6.x device
{
  "data": {
    "type": "jobs",
    "attributes": {
      "maxConnections": "10",
      "scheduleTime": "2017-05-13T04:31:28.211+0000",
      "scripts": [
        {
          "scriptName": "lagConfig",
          "inputs": [
            {
                "data": [
                {
                  "attributes": {
                    "action": "create",
                    "aggName":"ag",
                    "primaryPorts": "1",
                    "ethernetSettings": true
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "included": [
    {
      "id": "{{NE_NAME}}",
      "type": "connectionAttributes",
      "attributes": {
        "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Delete configured settings from network elements

Use Navigator MC’s Commissioning POST REST API of the Network Element Configuration to invoke requests.

POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/commissioning/function/remove

Delete configured settings from Network Elements.

Prerequisite: The following attributes should be specified in the post request

  • functionName - The Configuration function to be applied

  • neCommissioningDetails - Details of configured settings to be deleted from network elements

The examples below illustrate deletion of configured settings from network element.

{
  "data": {

          ]

    }

}
}
}

Queue Provisioning

Navigator MC provides native REST API with a distinct URL for queue configuration on the port . Through this API queue settings can be configured and updated independently from other commissioning/configuration operations.

  • Queues on a port can be configured.

  • Queues on a LAG port is supported for 6500 and 6x and for 10x it will be supported later as there is no LAG handoff for the 5170 as AN in the T-Mobile deployment.

Supported devices

Navigator MC supports this capability for the following devices:

  • 6500

  • Saos 6x

  • 5170 10.4 as AN at MSC site

New attributes introduced for 10x

  • schedulerName:- <portName>-Default [Note:- Absence of user input default value will be used ]

  • schedulerAlgorithm:-

    1. sp: strict priority[Note:- Default]

    2. rr: round robin

    3. wfq: weighted fair queueing

  • queueWeights:-
    [
    {
    "tapPoint":"value",
    "weight":"value",
    "priority":"value"
    }
    ]

where, priority with range value [0-7]

API call and examples

Use Navigator MC’s JOB POST REST API of the Network Element Configuration to invoke requests:

POST: /configmgmt/api/v1/queue/provisioning

Asynchronous notification after completion of the job will be available against the JOB_ID.

The examples below illustrate queue setting when provisioning queue on 10x device.

5170/5171/5144(SAOS 10x) Support

5170(SAOS 10.4) is supported as AN starting MCP 4.6.1 and 5171, 5144 (SAOS 10.5.1) is supported as AN starting MCP 4.6.3. This support is for Intra Metro. Below mentioned points are considerable with respect to 5170/5171/5144 support as AN.

  • With SAOS 10x devices supporting L3, it is expected to have any additional attributes being reported that are introduced as part of L3 support.

  • For seamless service over BGP-LU, only spoke PWs are supported over VPWS FDs in 5170/5171/5144.

  • For interop scenarios, VS mode can be 'VPLS, VPWS' for a service, where 3926 will have mode as VPLS and 5170/5171/5144 as VPWS.

  • 5170/5171/5144 does not supports cos-policy as fixed-cos. Same is achieved using Cutoms Maps. Only 4 custom maps are supported at device.

  • 5170/5171/5144 device displays ccm-interval of 3.33ms as 3.3ms (as per the Yang Model). Navigator MC will be converting 3.33ms to 3.3ms during provisioning and sync back 3.3ms as 3.33ms to maintain coherence with other device types.

  • LDP session for BGP-LU are shown to be created with 'mgmt' interface for 5170(SAOS 10.4). This is not functionally impacting.

MCP 4.6.2 introduces the support of Service Assurance for below:

  • CCM Status

  • CFM Loopback

  • Benchmark Reflector

  • Y.1731/MEF35.1 Responder

  • Alarm correlation for CFM Service Fault.

Configure CFM Down MEP & Y.1731 MEF35.1 delay on IP Interface

Configure CFM Down MEP & Y.1731 MEF35.1 delay on IP Interface using existing jobs API:

POST {BP_SERVER}/configmgmt/api/v1/jobs

Note: Supported devices for CFM down MEP configuration:

  • 6500-T 14.1+

  • 6500-S PTS 14.1+

Create CFM Down MEP service and optional Y.1731 MEF35.1 delay with IP interface

Refer Configure CFM Down MEP & Y.1731 MEF35.1 delay on IP Interface for API signature

Sample Request Payload

{
    "data": {
        "type": "jobs",
        "attributes": {
            "maxConnections": "10",
            "scripts": [
                {
                    "scriptName": "ipInterfacesConfig",
                    "inputs": [
                        {
                            "shelf": "{{SHELF}}",
                            "group": "{{GROUP}}",
                            "data": [
                              {
                                    "type": "ipInterfaces",
                                    "attributes": {
                                        "action": "create",
                                        "interfaceName": "Interface1",
                                        "cfmDownMep": {
                                            "cfmServiceName": "CFM1",
                                            "cfmAlarmPriority": 3,
                                            "cfmAlarmTime": 100,
                                            "cfmNextMepId": 3,
                                            "cfmResetTime": 200,
                                            "cfmRemoteMepAging": "on",
                                            "cfmRemoteMepAgingTime": 10,
                                            "cfmRemoteMepDiscovery": "off",
                                            "cfmSenderIdType": "manage",
                                            "cfmMdName": "md4",
                                            "cfmMaNameFormat": "integer",
                                            "cfmMaName": "400",
                                            "cfmCcmInterval": "3.33ms",
                                            "cfmDmmInterval": "10min",
                                            "cfmMepCcmLtmPriority": 7,
                                            "cfmMepCcmState": "on",
                                            "createCfmDelayProfile": true,
                                            "cfmDelayProfileName": "DelayProfile_1",
                                            "cfmDelayProfileStoredIntervalCount": 2,
                                            "isCfmDelayProfileAlignMeasurementInterval": true,
                                            "cfmDelayProfileAlignMeasurementOffset": 100,
                                            "createCfmMefDelay": true,
                                            "cfmLocalMepId": 100,
                                            "cfmRemoteMepId": 101,
                                            "cfmMefDmmTestId": 4294967295,
                                            "cfmMefDmmMeasurementInterval": 1440,
                                            "cfmMefDmmMessageInterval": "10min",
                                            "cfmMefDmmPriority": 7,
                                            "cfmMefDmmRepetitionTime": 525600,
                                            "cfmMefDmmFrameSize": 2000
                                        },
                                        "vlan": 7,
                                        "interfaceSvlanPriority": 7,
                                        "interfaceIpAddr": "10.1.1.1",
                                        "ip": "10.10.1.1",

                                        "port": "7/2",

    "included": [
        {
            "id": "{{NC_ID}}",
            "type": "connectionAttributes",
            "attributes": {
                "neName": "{{NE_NAME}}",
                "neType": "6500",
                "typeGroup": "Ciena6500"
            }
        }
    ]
}
